workflow_overview.name: nf-core/rnaseq
workflow_overview.purpose: Analyze RNA sequencing data from organisms with a reference genome and annotation to produce gene expression matrices and extensive quality control reports
key_features: Accepts FASTQ files or pre-aligned BAM files as input
BAM file reusability for downstream analysis

use_cases.scenario: Initial RNA-seq data processing from raw sequencing reads
use_cases.input_data: FASTQ files from RNA sequencing experiments
use_cases.expected_output: Gene expression matrix, aligned BAM files, quality control reports
use_cases.when_to_use: When starting with raw sequencing data that needs complete processing pipeline

use_cases.scenario: Reprocessing previously aligned data with different parameters
use_cases.input_data: Pre-aligned BAM files
use_cases.expected_output: Reprocessed alignments and quantifications with new parameters
use_cases.when_to_use: When you have existing BAM files and want to skip alignment step using --skip_alignment flag

use_cases.input_data: BAM files from previous pipeline runs
use_cases.expected_output: Quantification and quality control results
use_cases.when_to_use: When alignment is computationally expensive and you want to reuse existing BAM files

workflow_steps.purpose: Merge re-sequenced FastQ files
workflow_steps.input: Multiple FASTQ files from same sample
workflow_steps.why_needed: Samples sequenced multiple times need to be combined for unified analysis

workflow_steps.purpose: Auto-infer strandedness by subsampling and pseudoalignment
workflow_steps.why_needed: Strandedness is critical for accurate quantification and must be determined automatically or specified

workflow_steps.purpose: Read quality control assessment
workflow_steps.why_needed: Identifies quality issues in raw sequencing data before processing

workflow_steps.purpose: Extract Unique Molecular Identifiers
workflow_steps.why_needed: UMIs enable accurate deduplication and error correction in downstream analysis

workflow_steps.purpose: Adapter and quality trimming
workflow_steps.why_needed: Removes sequencing adapters and low-quality bases that interfere with alignment

workflow_steps.purpose: Removal of genome contaminants
workflow_steps.why_needed: Eliminates contaminating sequences from other organisms

workflow_steps.purpose: Removal of ribosomal RNA
workflow_steps.why_needed: rRNA comprises majority of RNA in cells but is not informative for gene expression analysis

workflow_steps.purpose: Alignment and quantification with multiple route options
workflow_steps.output: Aligned BAM files and/or quantification matrices
workflow_steps.why_needed: Maps reads to reference genome and quantifies transcript/gene expression. Multiple routes allow flexibility for different experimental designs

workflow_steps.purpose: Sort and index alignments
workflow_steps.why_needed: Sorting and indexing enables efficient downstream processing and visualization

workflow_steps.purpose: UMI-based deduplication
workflow_steps.input: Sorted BAM files with UMI information
workflow_steps.why_needed: Removes PCR duplicates identified by UMI sequences for accurate quantification

workflow_steps.purpose: Duplicate read marking
workflow_steps.why_needed: Identifies and marks PCR duplicates for downstream filtering and analysis

workflow_steps.purpose: Transcript assembly and quantification
workflow_steps.output: Transcript abundance estimates and GTF files
workflow_steps.why_needed: Assembles transcripts and quantifies their expression levels

workflow_steps.purpose: Create bigWig coverage files
workflow_steps.why_needed: Enables visualization of read coverage across genome in genome browsers

workflow_steps.purpose: Extensive quality control
workflow_steps.why_needed: Provides overview of data quality and pipeline performance across all steps

data_requirements.input_quality: High-quality RNA sequencing reads from organisms with reference genome and annotation available
data_requirements.file_organization: Samplesheet format required with FASTQ files or BAM files organized according to pipeline specifications

essential_parameters.name: input
essential_parameters.purpose: Specifies samplesheet with FASTQ or BAM files
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Always required - must point to valid samplesheet
essential_parameters.impact: Determines which samples are processed

essential_parameters.name: genome
essential_parameters.purpose: Specifies reference genome and annotation
essential_parameters.recommended_value: Valid genome identifier from iGenomes or custom path
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Must match organism being studied
essential_parameters.impact: Critical for accurate alignment and quantification

essential_parameters.name: aligner
essential_parameters.purpose: Selects alignment tool
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Based on experimental design and computational resources
essential_parameters.impact: Determines alignment quality and available quantification options

essential_parameters.name: pseudo_aligner
essential_parameters.purpose: Selects quantification tool when using STAR
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Based on desired quantification method
essential_parameters.impact: Affects gene expression quantification accuracy

essential_parameters.name: skip_alignment
essential_parameters.purpose: Skips alignment step when using pre-aligned BAM files
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: When reprocessing with existing BAM files
essential_parameters.impact: Saves significant computational time for reprocessing

common_issues.cause: Automatic strandedness detection may fail with certain library preparations
common_issues.solution: Manually specify strandedness parameter based on library preparation protocol
common_issues.prevention: Document library preparation method and verify strandedness inference results

best_practices: Use BAM files as input for reprocessing to avoid repeating computationally expensive alignment steps
Verify strandedness inference results match your library preparation protocol
Review MultiQC report to assess data quality across all pipeline steps
Organize input files according to samplesheet specifications before running pipeline
Consider using pre-aligned BAM files with --skip_alignment flag for downstream analysis without realignment

checkpoints: FastQC results on raw reads
Strandedness inference validation
Trimming efficiency assessment
Alignment quality metrics
Duplicate marking results
Coverage uniformity in BigWig files
red_flags: Strandedness inference conflicts with known protocol

primary_outputs.content: Quantified gene expression values across samples
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Input for downstream differential expression analysis, clustering, or other statistical analyses

primary_outputs.content: Reads mapped to reference genome with alignment information
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Can be reused as input for future runs with --skip_alignment flag; used for visualization and variant calling

primary_outputs.content: Genome-wide read coverage in BigWig format
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Visualization in genome browsers like IGV or UCSC Genome Browser

primary_outputs.content: Comprehensive quality control summary from all pipeline steps
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Assessment of data quality and pipeline performance; identification of problematic samples

primary_outputs.content: Transcript abundance estimates and assembled transcripts
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Transcript-level expression analysis and novel transcript discovery

output_interpretation.quality_reports: MultiQC report aggregating results from FastQC, alignment statistics, duplicate marking, and all other QC tools used in pipeline
output_interpretation.visualization: FastQC plots, coverage plots in BigWig format, MultiQC interactive visualizations, transcript abundance plots from StringTie

advantages: Comprehensive end-to-end pipeline from raw reads to expression matrix
Multiple alignment and quantification route options for flexibility
Automated strandedness inference
Extensive quality control and reporting
BAM file reusability for efficient reprocessing
Handles UMI-based deduplication
Removes common contaminants (rRNA, genome contaminants)
Produces publication-ready quality reports
limitations: Requires reference genome and annotation
HiSAT2 route does not include quantification
Documentation does not specify performance characteristics or cost estimates
comparison_to_alternatives.when_to_use_alternatives: When working with organisms without reference genomes, de novo assembly pipelines should be used instead

rnaseq.community_notes: BAM files produced by this pipeline can be efficiently reused as input for future runs with --skip_alignment flag, which is particularly useful for reprocessing data or running downstream analysis steps without repeating computationally expensive alignment. See usage documentation for details on using BAM files as input.

workflow_overview.name: nf-core/differentialabundance
workflow_overview.purpose: Analyze data represented as matrices by comparing groups of observations to generate differential statistics and downstream analyses
key_features: Support for RNA-seq data from nf-core rnaseq workflow
Support for Affymetrix arrays via .CEL files
Flexible matrix input for other data types
Comprehensive HTML reporting with interactive plots
Cross-validation of matrices, annotations, and contrasts

use_cases.input_data: Abundance matrix from nf-core rnaseq workflow, sample annotations, contrast definitions
use_cases.expected_output: Differential statistics, exploratory plots, differential plots, HTML report with interactive visualizations
use_cases.when_to_use: When comparing gene expression between experimental groups in RNA-seq studies

use_cases.input_data: Compressed CEL files archive (e.g., from GEO), sample annotations, contrast definitions
use_cases.expected_output: Differential statistics, quality control plots, HTML report
use_cases.when_to_use: When analyzing Affymetrix array data or data downloaded from GEO

use_cases.input_data: GSE study identifier for automatic SOFT file retrieval
use_cases.expected_output: Processed abundance data, differential statistics, comprehensive report
use_cases.when_to_use: When analyzing publicly available datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus

use_cases.input_data: TSV-format abundance matrix with custom data types
use_cases.expected_output: Differential statistics and visualizations
use_cases.when_to_use: When analyzing other types of matrix data with appropriate parameter adjustments

workflow_steps.purpose: Generate a list of genomic feature annotations from input GTF file
workflow_steps.why_needed: Provides genomic context and feature information for downstream analysis; optional if annotation table is explicitly supplied

workflow_steps.purpose: Cross-check matrices, sample annotations, feature sets, and contrasts for consistency
workflow_steps.input: Abundance matrix, sample sheet, feature annotations, contrast definitions
workflow_steps.why_needed: Ensures data integrity and prevents downstream errors from inconsistent inputs

workflow_steps.purpose: Run differential analysis over all specified contrasts
workflow_steps.input: Validated abundance matrix, sample annotations, contrast definitions
workflow_steps.why_needed: Core analysis step that generates statistical comparisons between sample groups

workflow_steps.purpose: Optionally run differential gene set analysis
workflow_steps.why_needed: Provides functional interpretation of differential results at pathway/gene set level

workflow_steps.purpose: Generate exploratory and differential analysis plots for interpretation
workflow_steps.why_needed: Enables visual exploration and communication of results

workflow_steps.purpose: Optionally build and deploy an interactive Shiny application
workflow_steps.output: Shiny app for interactive result mining
workflow_steps.why_needed: Provides interactive interface for exploring results without command-line access

workflow_steps.purpose: Build comprehensive HTML report with interactive plots and tables
workflow_steps.output: HTML report file named according to study_name parameter
workflow_steps.why_needed: Consolidates all results into shareable, reproducible report

input_formats: SOFT files from GEO (via GSE identifier)
data_requirements.input_quality: Matrices and annotations must be consistent and cross-validated; samples must be properly annotated
data_requirements.file_organization: Samples organized in comma-separated file with sample identifiers and metadata; contrasts defined in separate CSV file

essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Always set to identify your specific analysis
essential_parameters.impact: Determines output file names and report identification

essential_parameters.name: study_type

essential_parameters.impact: Determines appropriate analysis methods and parameters

essential_parameters.name: input

essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Required for every run
essential_parameters.impact: Defines which samples are included in analysis

essential_parameters.name: contrasts

essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Required for every run
essential_parameters.impact: Defines which group comparisons are performed

essential_parameters.name: outdir
essential_parameters.purpose: Output directory where results will be saved
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Required for every run
essential_parameters.impact: Determines where all results are written

essential_parameters.name: matrix
essential_parameters.purpose: TSV-format abundance matrix with samples and genes
essential_parameters.recommended_value: Absolute path to abundance matrix file
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Required unless using affy_cel_files_archive or querygse

essential_parameters.name: observations_id_col

essential_parameters.name: observations_type

workflow_overview.name: nf-core/methylseq
workflow_overview.purpose: Bioinformatics analysis pipeline for Methylation (Bisulfite) sequencing data that pre-processes raw data from FastQ inputs, aligns reads, and performs extensive quality-control
key_features: Support for multiple alignment tools (Bismark, bwa-meth, MethylDackel)
BWA-MEM2 support for faster CPU runs
MultiQC integration for comprehensive result summarization
Container-based reproducibility (Docker, Singularity, Podman, Charliecloud, Apptainer)

use_cases.input_data: FastQ files from bisulfite-treated DNA sequencing
use_cases.expected_output: Aligned BAM files, methylation calls, quality reports
use_cases.when_to_use: When studying genome-wide DNA methylation patterns

use_cases.input_data: FastQ files from bisulfite sequencing
use_cases.expected_output: Aligned BAM files with methylation annotations
use_cases.when_to_use: When computational speed is critical and GPU resources are available

use_cases.scenario: Comparative methylation studies across multiple samples
use_cases.input_data: Multiple FastQ files from re-sequenced samples
use_cases.expected_output: Merged and aligned results with quality metrics
use_cases.when_to_use: When analyzing methylation patterns across sample cohorts

workflow_steps.purpose: Create indexed reference genome for alignment
workflow_steps.why_needed: Required for efficient read alignment; different aligners require different index formats

workflow_steps.purpose: Merge re-sequenced FastQ files
workflow_steps.input: Multiple FastQ files from same sample
workflow_steps.why_needed: Consolidates multiple sequencing runs of the same sample for unified analysis

workflow_steps.purpose: Raw data quality control
workflow_steps.why_needed: Assesses sequencing quality before alignment to identify potential issues

workflow_steps.purpose: Align bisulfite-treated reads to reference genome
workflow_steps.input: Merged FastQ files, indexed reference genome
workflow_steps.why_needed: Three-base aligners specifically designed for bisulfite sequencing data where unmethylated cytosines appear as thymines

workflow_steps.purpose: Extract methylation calls from aligned reads
workflow_steps.why_needed: Converts alignment information into methylation status at individual cytosines

workflow_steps.purpose: Aggregate and summarize quality control results
workflow_steps.input: QC reports from all pipeline steps
workflow_steps.why_needed: Provides unified view of pipeline results and quality metrics across all samples

data_requirements.input_quality: High-quality bisulfite-treated sequencing data; FastQC should show appropriate quality scores
data_requirements.minimum_samples: 1 sample minimum, though typically multiple samples for comparative studies
data_requirements.file_organization: FastQ files organized for sample identification; re-sequenced samples can be merged automatically

essential_parameters.name: --aligner
essential_parameters.purpose: Selects alignment tool and workflow
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Use 'bismark_hisat' for HISAT2-based alignment; use 'bwameth' for bwa-meth/MethylDackel workflow
essential_parameters.impact: Determines entire downstream analysis pipeline and output format

essential_parameters.name: --use_mem2
essential_parameters.purpose: Enables BWA-MEM2 algorithm for faster CPU performance
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Enable when using bwameth aligner on CPU and speed is important
essential_parameters.impact: Significantly improves runtime for bwa-meth alignment on CPU systems

essential_parameters.name: -profile gpu
essential_parameters.purpose: Enables GPU acceleration via Parabricks
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: Include when GPU resources available and using bwameth aligner
essential_parameters.impact: Enables high-performance GPU-accelerated alignment using fq2bammeth (Parabricks implementation)

performance_tuning.compute_requirements: Varies by aligner and dataset size; GPU profile requires GPU hardware; CPU runs benefit from multi-core systems
performance_tuning.cost_considerations: Pipeline tested on AWS cloud infrastructure with sensible resource allocation defaults for real-world datasets

common_issues.problem: GPU pathway not working with Conda/Mamba
common_issues.cause: Parabricks GPU implementation requires container runtime
common_issues.solution: Use Docker, Singularity, or Podman instead of Conda/Mamba for GPU profile
common_issues.prevention: Always use container runtime when running with -profile gpu

best_practices: Choose aligner based on computational resources: Bismark for standard CPU, bwameth with --use_mem2 for faster CPU, Parabricks with -profile gpu for GPU acceleration
Run FastQC quality control before committing to full pipeline analysis
Use container-based execution (Docker/Singularity/Podman) for reproducibility across different compute environments
Review MultiQC report for comprehensive quality assessment across all samples
Understand bisulfite sequencing and three-base aligner principles before interpreting results
Test pipeline on full-sized datasets to ensure proper resource allocation

checkpoints: FastQC quality assessment of raw FastQ files
Alignment statistics and coverage metrics
Methylation call quality and distribution
MultiQC aggregated quality report
red_flags: Low alignment rates indicating poor quality or contamination

primary_outputs.content: Reads aligned to reference genome with methylation information
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Input for methylation extraction and downstream analysis

primary_outputs.content: Methylation status at individual cytosines
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Direct input for methylation analysis, visualization, and statistical testing

primary_outputs.content: Aggregated quality control metrics and visualizations
primary_outputs.how_to_use: Review for overall pipeline quality and sample-level metrics

output_interpretation.quality_reports: FastQC reports for raw data quality; alignment statistics; methylation extraction reports; comprehensive MultiQC summary
output_interpretation.visualization: Quality score distributions, alignment rate plots, coverage plots, methylation distribution plots, and other metrics visualized in MultiQC report

advantages: Supports multiple alignment tools allowing flexibility based on computational resources
GPU acceleration option for high-performance analysis
Comprehensive quality control integrated throughout pipeline
Reproducible results via containerization

Automated continuous integration testing on AWS

workflow_overview.name: nf-core/sarek
workflow_overview.purpose: Detect variants on whole genome or targeted sequencing data from single samples or tumor/normal pairs with optional relapses
key_features: Multi-species support (initially Human and Mouse, extensible to any species with reference genome)
Tumor/normal pair analysis with relapse support
Multiple alignment algorithms (BWA-mem, BWA-mem2, dragmap, Sentieon BWA-mem, parabricks)
Comprehensive BAM processing with quality control

use_cases.scenario: Whole genome sequencing variant detection in human samples
use_cases.input_data: FastQ files or BAM files from WGS experiments
use_cases.expected_output: Variant calls, processed BAM files, alignment statistics, quality control reports
use_cases.when_to_use: Standard germline variant discovery in human populations

use_cases.input_data: FastQ or BAM files from tumor and matched normal samples
use_cases.expected_output: Somatic variant calls, tumor-specific variants, quality metrics
use_cases.when_to_use: Cancer genomics studies requiring somatic mutation detection

use_cases.input_data: FastQ files from targeted sequencing panels
use_cases.expected_output: Variant calls for targeted regions, coverage statistics
use_cases.when_to_use: Gene panel sequencing or exome sequencing projects

use_cases.input_data: FastQ or BAM files from primary tumor and multiple relapse samples
use_cases.expected_output: Variant evolution tracking, relapse-specific mutations
use_cases.when_to_use: Longitudinal cancer studies tracking clonal evolution

essential_parameters.purpose: Number of base pairs to remove from 5' end of read 1 (or single-end reads)

essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: When FastQC shows quality issues at 5' end or known adapter sequences present
essential_parameters.impact: Removes problematic sequence; excessive clipping reduces usable read length

essential_parameters.name: clip_r2
essential_parameters.purpose: Number of base pairs to remove from 5' end of read 2 (paired-end only)
essential_parameters.recommended_value: 0 (default); adjust if known adapter or low-quality sequence at 5' end
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: When FastQC shows quality issues at 5' end of read 2
essential_parameters.impact: Removes problematic sequence from second read; excessive clipping reduces usable read length

essential_parameters.name: three_prime_clip_r1
essential_parameters.purpose: Number of base pairs to remove from 3' end of read 1 AFTER adapter/quality trimming
essential_parameters.recommended_value: 0 (default); adjust if quality degrades at 3' end
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: When FastQC shows quality degradation at 3' end after initial trimming

essential_parameters.name: three_prime_clip_r2
essential_parameters.purpose: Number of base pairs to remove from 3' end of read 2 AFTER adapter/quality trimming
essential_parameters.recommended_value: 0 (default); adjust if quality degrades at 3' end
essential_parameters.when_to_adjust: When FastQC shows quality degradation at 3' end of read 2
essential_parameters.impact: Final trimming step for read 2; removes low-quality 3' ends

essential_parameters.impact: Enables NextSeq-specific quality trimming; improves read quality for NextSeq data

proteomicslfq.community_notes: Pipeline follows nf-core standards and best practices. subworkflow_overview.name: QUANTIFY_PSEUDO_ALIGNMENT

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_ALIGN_DEDUP_BWAMEM

component_tools.role: Performs initial alignment of FASTQ reads to reference genome using BWA-MEM algorithm with automatic sorting

Add read group information to BAM headers
Identify and mark/remove PCR duplicate reads
Create index for deduplicated BAM file

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_ALIGN_DEDUP_BISMARK

ANGSD execution errors due to invalid parameters
recovery_actions: Regenerate BAI index files using samtools index
Verify HapMap file format and genome build compatibility
Check BAM file coverage statistics and adjust ANGSD parameters if needed
Review ANGSD error logs and validate input file integrity

subworkflow_overview.name: BCL_DEMULTIPLEX
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Demultiplex Illumina BCL (Binary Call Format) data into FASTQ files using either bcl-convert or bcl2fastq tools
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: start/early stage - processes raw sequencing output before quality control and analysis
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: BCL files from Illumina sequencer, valid samplesheet.csv with demultiplexing information, flowcell metadata

component_tools.role: Modern Illumina demultiplexer that converts BCL files to FASTQ format with interop and reports output
component_tools.why_chosen: Newer tool with improved performance and features for recent Illumina platforms

component_tools.role: Legacy Illumina demultiplexer that converts BCL files to FASTQ format, also generates stats output
component_tools.why_chosen: Maintained for backward compatibility with older sequencing runs and established workflows

data_flow.input: ch_flowcell containing [metadata with id and lane, samplesheet.csv path, BCL files as either tar.gz archive or directory path]
transformations: Branch flowcells into tar archives and directory paths
Decompress tar archives if needed
Merge metadata with samplesheets and run directories
Execute selected demultiplexer (bclconvert or bcl2fastq)
Transpose FASTQ output from [meta, [fastq_array]] to individual [meta, fastq] tuples
Parse FASTQ headers to extract sample ID, sample name, flowcell ID, and lane information
Read first line of gzipped FASTQ to validate format and extract metadata
data_flow.output: ch_fastq (demultiplexed FASTQ files with enriched metadata), ch_reports (demultiplexing reports), ch_interop (interop files), ch_stats (bcl2fastq only), ch_versions (tool versions)
data_flow.format_conversions: BCL binary format → FASTQ text format (gzip compressed), tar.gz archives → extracted directories

use_patterns.scenario: Processing recent Illumina sequencing runs with modern instruments
use_patterns.upstream: Raw BCL output from NovaSeq, NextSeq, or iSeq platforms
use_patterns.downstream: Quality control (FastQC), adapter trimming, alignment, or variant calling
use_patterns.variations: Use bclconvert parameter for optimal performance with current platforms

use_patterns.scenario: Processing legacy sequencing runs or maintaining backward compatibility
use_patterns.upstream: BCL output from older MiSeq, HiSeq, or GAIIx platforms
use_patterns.downstream: Quality control, trimming, alignment workflows
use_patterns.variations: Use bcl2fastq parameter; stats output available for additional QC metrics

use_patterns.scenario: Handling compressed flowcell archives from cloud storage or archival systems
use_patterns.upstream: Tar-gzipped BCL directories
use_patterns.downstream: Standard demultiplexing and analysis
use_patterns.variations: Subworkflow automatically detects and decompresses tar.gz files without manual intervention

parameter_interactions.interaction: Controls which tool is executed; value must be either 'bclconvert' or 'bcl2fastq'. Only one tool runs per execution. bcl2fastq additionally outputs stats channel
Format [meta, samplesheet, run] is branched based on run file type (.tar.gz vs directory), then merged back before tool execution

checks_performed: FASTQ header validation - verifies first line starts with '@' character
GZIP stream integrity - reads through gzipped FASTQ without decompression to local disk
Metadata extraction from FASTQ headers - parses Illumina CASAVA 1.8+ format with colon-delimited fields
Sample ID extraction - removes R1/R2 read indicators and S[number] sample identifiers from filenames
failure_modes: Invalid or corrupted FASTQ files (header validation fails)
Malformed samplesheet preventing demultiplexing
Tar archive corruption or incomplete extraction
Mismatched metadata between flowcell and samplesheet
Unsupported demultiplexer parameter value
recovery_actions: Validate samplesheet format against Illumina specifications before execution
Verify BCL file integrity and tar archive checksums
Check flowcell metadata (id, lane) matches samplesheet entries
Ensure demultiplexer parameter is exactly 'bclconvert' or 'bcl2fastq'
Review tool-specific error logs in reports output for detailed failure information

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTA_VCLUST_PREFILTER_ALIGN_CLUSTER
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Executes a three-stage VCLUST clustering pipeline to identify and group similar sequences based on genomic similarity metrics (ANI, GANI, TANI)
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/end of comparative genomics or metagenomic analysis pipelines
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Input FASTA sequences must be provided; VCLUST tools must be installed and accessible

component_tools.role: First stage: creates a prefilter of candidate sequence pairs to reduce computational burden in alignment stage
component_tools.why_chosen: Efficient candidate pair generation optimized for VCLUST pipeline; reduces downstream alignment computation

component_tools.role: Second stage: computes pairwise alignments and calculates similarity metrics (ANI, GANI, TANI) between candidate pairs
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized for genomic similarity calculations; integrates seamlessly with VCLUST clustering metrics

component_tools.role: Third stage: generates threshold-based clusters using similarity metrics from alignment stage
component_tools.why_chosen: Applies user-defined thresholds on ANI/GANI/TANI metrics for reproducible, interpretable clustering

data_flow.input: ch_fasta (channel with metadata and FASTA files), save_alignment (boolean), metric (string), tani/gani/ani (float thresholds)
transformations: VCLUST_PREFILTER generates candidate pair list (txt format)
Join prefilter output with original FASTA using metadata
VCLUST_ALIGN processes FASTA and filter pairs, produces alignment metrics (tsv, ids, optional aln)
VCLUST_CLUSTER applies thresholds to alignment metrics, generates cluster assignments
Join cluster output with original FASTA for final output
data_flow.output: fasta (original sequences), clusters (TSV cluster assignments), alignment (ALN files if save_alignment=true), ids (sequence identifiers), versions (tool versions)
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTA → prefilter TXT → alignment TSV/IDS → cluster TSV; optional ALN alignment format

use_patterns.scenario: Clustering genomes by genomic similarity in comparative genomics studies
use_patterns.upstream: Quality-filtered FASTA sequences from assembly or database
use_patterns.downstream: Cluster-based analysis, representative sequence selection, phylogenetic analysis
use_patterns.variations: Adjusting ANI/GANI/TANI thresholds for different taxonomic levels; enabling/disabling alignment output

use_patterns.upstream: Assembled contigs or MAGs in FASTA format
use_patterns.downstream: Representative genome selection, abundance profiling
use_patterns.variations: Strict thresholds (95% ANI) for species-level clustering; relaxed thresholds for genus-level grouping

use_patterns.scenario: Large-scale sequence clustering with computational efficiency
use_patterns.upstream: Bulk FASTA files from genomic databases
use_patterns.downstream: Cluster statistics, network analysis
use_patterns.variations: Disabling alignment output (save_alignment=false) to reduce storage; using different metrics (ANI vs GANI)

parameter_interactions.interaction: Specifies which similarity metric (ANI, GANI, or TANI) is used as primary clustering criterion; must match metrics computed by VCLUST_ALIGN
Float thresholds applied to respective metrics; clusters are formed when pairwise similarity exceeds specified threshold; lower values create larger clusters
Boolean flag controlling whether alignment files (ALN format) are generated and emitted; set to false to reduce storage/compute when alignments not needed

checks_performed: Metadata synchronization via join operations ensures FASTA and filter files remain paired across stages
Version tracking from each module for reproducibility and dependency documentation
Prefilter output validation ensures candidate pairs are generated before alignment
Alignment metric computation validates similarity calculations before clustering
failure_modes: Mismatched metadata between FASTA and prefilter output causing join failures
Invalid threshold parameters (tani/gani/ani) producing empty or over-clustered results
Insufficient prefilter candidates leading to sparse alignment results
Memory exhaustion on large FASTA files during alignment stage
recovery_actions: Verify input FASTA metadata consistency and format
Adjust similarity thresholds based on expected sequence divergence
Tune prefilter parameters if candidate generation is insufficient
Process large datasets in batches or increase computational resources

subworkflow_overview.name: bam_stats_samtools
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Generates comprehensive alignment statistics from SAM/BAM/CRAM files using three complementary SAMtools utilities to assess mapping quality, read distribution, and coverage
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/end of pipeline - post-alignment quality control and assessment
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Aligned BAM/CRAM files with corresponding index files (.bai/.crai) and reference FASTA sequence

component_tools.role: Generates detailed statistical summary of alignment file including read counts, quality scores, insert sizes, and base composition
component_tools.why_chosen: Comprehensive statistics with reference-aware analysis; lightweight and fast

component_tools.role: Produces concise summary of read flags (paired, mapped, duplicates, QC-failed) for quick quality assessment
component_tools.why_chosen: Fast, standardized flag-based counting; essential for mapping rate assessment

component_tools.role: Reports per-chromosome/contig read counts and unmapped reads for coverage distribution analysis
component_tools.why_chosen: Requires only index file; provides rapid per-contig statistics without full file scan

data_flow.input: BAM/CRAM files with index files (ch_bam_bai: [meta, bam, bai]) and reference FASTA (ch_fasta: [meta, fasta])
transformations: SAMTOOLS_STATS processes alignment with reference to generate detailed statistics
SAMTOOLS_FLAGSTAT analyzes read flags for mapping summary
SAMTOOLS_IDXSTATS queries index for per-contig coverage
data_flow.output: Three independent statistics files (stats, flagstat, idxstats) plus version tracking
data_flow.format_conversions: Binary BAM/CRAM → text-based statistics files (.stats, .flagstat, .idxstats)

use_patterns.upstream: BAM sorting and indexing (samtools sort, samtools index)
use_patterns.downstream: MultiQC aggregation, report generation, or conditional filtering based on statistics
use_patterns.variations: Can be applied to multiple samples in parallel; statistics used for sample-level QC decisions

use_patterns.upstream: Multiple aligned BAM files from same or different experiments
use_patterns.downstream: Statistical comparison of mapping rates, coverage uniformity across cohorts
use_patterns.variations: Output aggregated for cross-sample metrics

use_patterns.upstream: Initial alignment results showing unexpected quality
use_patterns.downstream: Investigation of per-contig coverage, flag distributions to identify systematic problems
use_patterns.variations: Detailed stats examination for specific regions or read classes

parameter_interactions.interaction: Required only by SAMTOOLS_STATS for reference-aware analysis; FLAGSTAT and IDXSTATS operate independently on index/file
IDXSTATS requires valid index for rapid access; FLAGSTAT can work without but index improves performance
Propagated through all tools to maintain sample identity and enable downstream aggregation

checks_performed: Mapping rate assessment via flagstat (percentage of mapped reads)
Per-contig coverage distribution via idxstats (identifies coverage gaps or anomalies)
Overall alignment quality metrics via stats (insert size, base quality, GC content)
Duplicate read detection via flagstat (identifies PCR bias)
failure_modes: Corrupted or incomplete BAM file causing stats generation failure
Missing or mismatched index file preventing IDXSTATS execution
Reference FASTA mismatch causing STATS discrepancies
Extremely low mapping rates indicating alignment failure
Highly skewed per-contig coverage suggesting systematic bias
recovery_actions: Validate BAM integrity with 'samtools quickcheck'
Regenerate index with 'samtools index' if missing
Verify reference FASTA matches alignment reference
Review alignment parameters if mapping rate <80%
Investigate library preparation or sequencing issues if coverage highly non-uniform

subworkflow_overview.name: bam_create_som_pon_gatk
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Create a GATK-based somatic panel of normals (PoN) by performing variant calling on normal samples using MuTect2, aggregating variants into a GenomicsDB workspace, and generating a final PoN VCF
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/preprocessing stage - typically runs once during pipeline setup or as a separate preparatory step before somatic variant calling
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: BAM files from normal samples with corresponding indices, reference genome (FASTA), FAI index, sequence dictionary, and interval files for genomic regions of interest

component_tools.role: Performs variant calling on each normal sample in panel-of-normals mode to identify potential somatic variants
component_tools.why_chosen: MuTect2 is specifically designed for somatic variant detection and has a dedicated PoN mode that filters germline variants

component_tools.role: Aggregates VCF files from all samples into a GenomicsDB workspace for efficient multi-sample variant storage and querying
component_tools.why_chosen: GenomicsDB provides optimized storage and retrieval for large-scale variant databases, essential for PoN construction

component_tools.role: Generates the final panel of normals VCF from the GenomicsDB workspace, filtering variants to create a high-confidence PoN resource
component_tools.why_chosen: GATK's dedicated tool applies appropriate statistical filters and normalization for somatic PoN creation

data_flow.input: ch_mutect2_in (BAM files with indices and intervals), ch_fasta (reference genome), ch_fai (FASTA index), ch_dict (sequence dictionary), val_pon_norm (PoN name string), ch_gendb_intervals (interval files for GenomicsDB)
transformations: MuTect2 variant calling on each normal sample independently producing per-sample VCFs
Collection and aggregation of all sample VCFs and indices into lists
Construction of GenomicsDB input channel combining VCFs, indices, intervals, and reference metadata
GenomicsDB workspace creation from aggregated variants
Panel of normals VCF generation from GenomicsDB workspace with reference-based filtering
data_flow.output: mutect2_vcf (per-sample VCFs), mutect2_index (per-sample TBI indices), mutect2_stats (MuTect2 statistics), genomicsdb (GenomicsDB workspace), pon_vcf (final PoN VCF), pon_index (PoN VCF index), versions (tool versions)
data_flow.format_conversions: BAM → VCF (MuTect2), VCF → GenomicsDB (GenomicsDBImport), GenomicsDB → VCF (CreateSomaticPanelOfNormals)

use_patterns.scenario: Creating a project-specific panel of normals from in-house normal samples
use_patterns.upstream: BAM alignment and quality control of normal samples
use_patterns.downstream: Use generated PoN VCF as input to somatic variant calling workflows (e.g., MuTect2 tumor-normal calling with --panel-of-normals parameter)
use_patterns.variations: Can be run once and reused across multiple projects; interval files can be whole-genome or targeted regions

use_patterns.scenario: Building organism or cohort-specific PoN resources
use_patterns.upstream: Collection of representative normal samples from target population
use_patterns.downstream: Distribution of PoN as reference resource for downstream analyses
use_patterns.variations: Sample count can range from 10s to 1000s; GenomicsDB workspace can be updated incrementally with new samples

parameter_interactions.interaction: String identifier used as metadata ID throughout GenomicsDB and final PoN VCF, enabling traceability and versioning of PoN resources
Defines genomic regions included in GenomicsDB workspace; restricting intervals reduces database size and processing time but may miss variants outside regions
Ensures consistent contig ordering and naming across all tools; mismatches cause failures in variant aggregation

checks_performed: MuTect2 produces valid VCF with proper headers and variant records
All sample VCFs successfully indexed with TBI
GenomicsDB workspace creation completes without corruption
Final PoN VCF contains expected variant count and passes GATK validation
failure_modes: MuTect2 fails on individual samples due to BAM corruption or reference mismatch
GenomicsDB import fails if VCF headers are inconsistent across samples
CreateSomaticPanelOfNormals produces empty or minimal PoN if variant filtering is too stringent
Memory exhaustion during GenomicsDB creation with very large sample counts
recovery_actions: Validate input BAM files with samtools quickcheck before workflow execution
Ensure all samples use identical reference genome and sequence dictionary
Review MuTect2 filtering parameters if PoN is unexpectedly sparse
Increase memory allocation or split GenomicsDB creation by chromosome for large cohorts

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_QC_TRIM_FILTER_SETSTRANDEDNESS
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Performs comprehensive quality control, trimming, filtering, and RNA-seq library strandedness determination on FASTQ files to prepare them for downstream analysis
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: Early in RNA-seq pipeline, immediately after raw FASTQ input
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Raw FASTQ files from sequencing; optional rRNA reference databases for filtering; optional UMI information in reads

component_tools.role: Validates FASTQ file format integrity at multiple stages (initial, post-trimming, post-bbsplit, post-sortmerna)
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight format validation at each processing stage to catch corruption early

component_tools.role: Performs quality control assessment and adapter/quality trimming with optional UMI extraction
component_tools.why_chosen: Comprehensive QC with trim_galore for standard trimming workflows

component_tools.role: Alternative fast trimming and QC with UMI support and built-in filtering
component_tools.why_chosen: Faster alternative for high-throughput processing

component_tools.role: Filters out ribosomal RNA (rRNA) sequences to reduce non-coding RNA contamination
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized rRNA filtering with indexing capability

component_tools.role: Separates reads by genomic origin (e.g., host vs pathogen, or multiple genomes)
component_tools.why_chosen: Flexible multi-genome read splitting

component_tools.role: Subsamples reads and performs Salmon quantification to infer library strandedness
component_tools.why_chosen: Efficient strandedness inference via Salmon's lib_format_counts.json output

component_tools.role: Concatenates FASTQ files from multiple lanes or samples
component_tools.why_chosen: Handles Nextflow channel concatenation properly

data_flow.input: Raw FASTQ files [meta, reads] where meta contains sample metadata and reads are FASTQ file paths
transformations: Initial format validation with FQ_LINT
Quality control and trimming via trimgalore or fastp
Post-trimming format validation
Optional rRNA filtering with SORTMERNA
Optional genome separation with BBMAP_BBSPLIT
Subsampling and Salmon quantification for strandedness inference
Strandedness calculation from Salmon lib_format_counts.json
Final format validation
data_flow.output: Trimmed, filtered FASTQ files with inferred strandedness metadata [meta, trimmed_reads, strandedness_info]
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTQ → validated FASTQ → trimmed FASTQ → filtered FASTQ; JSON (Salmon output) → strandedness classification

use_patterns.upstream: Raw FASTQ files from sequencer
use_patterns.downstream: Alignment with STAR or Hisat2 using inferred strandedness
use_patterns.variations: Enable SORTMERNA filtering, use trimgalore for conservative trimming

use_patterns.upstream: Raw FASTQ with UMI barcodes in read names or sequences
use_patterns.downstream: UMI-aware alignment and deduplication
use_patterns.variations: Use FASTQ_FASTQC_UMITOOLS_FASTP with UMI extraction enabled

use_patterns.upstream: Mixed FASTQ from co-infection or contamination
use_patterns.downstream: Separate alignment pipelines for each genome
use_patterns.variations: Enable BBMAP_BBSPLIT with multiple reference genomes

use_patterns.upstream: Trimmed FASTQ files
use_patterns.downstream: Strand-aware quantification and differential expression
use_patterns.variations: Adjust stranded_threshold and unstranded_threshold parameters for sensitivity

parameter_interactions.interaction: If forward or reverse proportion >= 0.8, library classified as stranded; lower values increase sensitivity to detect weak strandedness
If absolute difference between forward/reverse proportions <= 0.1, library classified as unstranded; lower values require more balanced proportions
Choice affects trimming aggressiveness, speed, and UMI handling; fastp is faster but trimgalore more conservative
When enabled, reads are filtered against rRNA databases; requires rRNA reference index; adds processing time but reduces contamination
When enabled, reads split into separate files by genome; requires multiple reference genomes; output channels split accordingly

checks_performed: FASTQ format validation at 4 stages (initial, post-trim, post-bbsplit, post-sortmerna)
FastQC quality metrics on raw and trimmed reads
Adapter contamination detection and removal
Quality score distribution analysis
Read length distribution post-trimming
rRNA contamination quantification
Strandedness inference confidence via Salmon fragment counts
failure_modes: Corrupted FASTQ files detected by FQ_LINT - stops pipeline
Insufficient reads for strandedness inference - returns 'undetermined'
All fragments unstranded (edge case) - returns 'undetermined'
Extreme quality scores or adapter contamination - may require parameter adjustment
rRNA index missing when SORTMERNA enabled - pipeline fails
Salmon quantification fails - strandedness cannot be inferred
recovery_actions: Re-run with stricter quality thresholds if contamination detected
Increase subsample size if strandedness undetermined
Adjust stranded_threshold/unstranded_threshold parameters for borderline cases
Provide rRNA reference databases if filtering enabled
Use alternative trimmer (fastp vs trimgalore) if one fails
Manually specify strandedness if inference fails but library type known

subworkflow_overview.name: VCF_EXTRACT_RELATE_SOMALIER
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Perform somalier extraction and relatedness analysis on input VCFs to identify sample relationships and generate statistical reports
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/end of pipeline
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Input VCFs (with or without tabix indices), reference FASTA with index, somalier sites VCF, and PED files for sample relationships

component_tools.role: Index VCF files that lack tabix indices before somalier processing
component_tools.why_chosen: Standard indexing tool for VCF files; required for somalier extract to function properly

component_tools.role: Extract genotype information from VCFs at somalier sites for each sample
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized tool optimized for extracting relevant genetic markers for relatedness analysis

component_tools.role: Compute pairwise relatedness statistics and generate HTML reports and TSV outputs
component_tools.why_chosen: Fast, accurate relatedness computation with integrated visualization and optional sample grouping

data_flow.input: VCFs with metadata and optional indices, reference FASTA with FAI index, somalier sites VCF, PED files, optional sample groups file, optional common identifier string
transformations: Branch VCFs into those with and without tabix indices
Index VCFs lacking indices using TABIX_TABIX
Join indexed VCFs with original VCF metadata
Extract somalier genotypes from all VCFs using reference and sites
Group extracted samples by count (for multi-sample VCFs) or by common ID (for single-sample VCFs)
Join grouped extracts with PED files
Sort extract files alphabetically by filename
Remove GroupKey wrapper and flatten extract lists
Compute relatedness statistics and generate reports
data_flow.output: Extract files per sample, HTML relatedness report, pairs TSV with pairwise statistics, samples TSV with sample-level statistics, version information
data_flow.format_conversions: VCF → indexed VCF → somalier extract format → relatedness statistics (TSV/HTML)

use_patterns.scenario: Multi-sample VCF analysis with known pedigrees
use_patterns.upstream: VCF calling/merging pipeline producing multi-sample VCFs
use_patterns.downstream: Quality control reports, sample swap detection, pedigree validation
use_patterns.variations: Can use count parameter to group samples; PED file provides expected relationships

use_patterns.scenario: Single-sample VCF analysis requiring sample grouping
use_patterns.upstream: Individual sample VCF calling
use_patterns.downstream: Cross-sample relatedness analysis, batch QC reports
use_patterns.variations: Requires val_common_id parameter to group single-sample VCFs; optional sample_groups file for categorization

use_patterns.scenario: VCF files with pre-existing tabix indices
use_patterns.upstream: Previously indexed VCF files
use_patterns.downstream: Direct somalier extraction without re-indexing
use_patterns.variations: Branching logic skips TABIX_TABIX for indexed files, improving efficiency

parameter_interactions.interaction: When provided, overrides metadata ID with value from specified metadata field; enables grouping of single-sample VCFs; when absent, uses original metadata ID for multi-sample VCFs
When count > 0, creates GroupKey to group multiple samples from same VCF; when count = 0 or absent, treats each sample independently
Optional file passed to SOMALIER_RELATE for sample categorization in relatedness analysis; affects report organization and visualization
Defines which genomic positions to extract; critical for consistent relatedness computation across all samples

checks_performed: VCF indexing validation (TABIX_TABIX ensures proper index format)
Metadata matching with failOnDuplicate and failOnMismatch flags in joins
Somalier extract file generation and sorting for consistency
Pedigree file validation through join operation
failure_modes: Missing or corrupted VCF indices causing TABIX_TABIX to fail
Metadata mismatches between VCF channel and PED channel triggering join failures
Inconsistent sample naming between VCFs and PED files
Invalid val_common_id parameter not matching metadata field names
Somalier sites VCF incompatible with input VCF reference genome
recovery_actions: Ensure input VCFs are valid and reference genome matches somalier sites VCF
Verify PED file sample IDs match VCF sample names exactly
Confirm val_common_id parameter matches actual metadata field names
Check somalier sites VCF is appropriate for reference genome build
Validate count parameter and grouping logic for single vs multi-sample VCFs

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTA_HMMSEARCH_RANK_FASTAS
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Search protein/DNA sequences against HMM profiles, rank hits by score, and extract top-scoring sequences into separate FASTA files per profile
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline - post-sequence preparation, pre-downstream analysis
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: HMM profile files and a reference FASTA sequence file must be available; HMMER and seqtk tools must be installed

component_tools.role: Searches input FASTA sequences against each HMM profile to identify homologous sequences and generate target summary statistics
component_tools.why_chosen: HMMER is optimized for profile-based sequence searching with statistical significance scoring; produces structured output suitable for ranking

component_tools.role: Aggregates and ranks all hmmsearch results across multiple profiles, consolidating target summary files into a single ranked TSV output
component_tools.why_chosen: Purpose-built HMMER utility that standardizes ranking across multiple profile searches with consistent scoring metrics

component_tools.role: Extracts specific sequences from the original FASTA file based on accession numbers of top-ranked hits
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight, fast sequence extraction tool that efficiently retrieves subsequences by ID from large FASTA files

data_flow.input: ch_hmms: channel of [meta, hmm_file] tuples (multiple HMM profiles); ch_fasta: single FASTA file containing sequences to search
transformations: Combine each HMM profile with the FASTA file and configure hmmsearch parameters (false, true, false flags)
Run hmmsearch for each profile against all sequences, generating target_summary outputs
Collect all target_summary files and pass to hmmrank for consolidated ranking
Parse hmmrank TSV output, filter for rank==1 (top hit per profile), extract accession numbers
Group accession numbers by profile name into separate filter files
Combine filter files with original FASTA and pass to seqtk_subseq for extraction
data_flow.output: hmmrank: consolidated TSV ranking all hits across profiles; seqfastas: [meta, fasta] tuples with extracted top-scoring sequences per profile
data_flow.format_conversions: hmmsearch output (text) → target_summary (tabular) → hmmrank TSV (tabular) → accession lists (text) → extracted FASTA (sequence)

use_patterns.scenario: Identifying best homologs across multiple protein families
use_patterns.upstream: HMM profile generation/curation, FASTA sequence database preparation
use_patterns.downstream: Sequence alignment, phylogenetic analysis, functional annotation of top hits
use_patterns.variations: Filtering by E-value threshold before ranking, extracting top-N hits instead of rank==1, processing multiple FASTA files sequentially

use_patterns.scenario: Quality control in genome annotation pipelines
use_patterns.upstream: Gene prediction, ORF calling
use_patterns.downstream: Validation against known protein families, contamination detection
use_patterns.variations: Using domain-specific HMM databases (Pfam, TIGRFAM), adjusting hmmsearch sensitivity parameters

parameter_interactions.interaction: Controls search mode and output format; these flags likely control: domain reporting, per-sequence reporting, and output verbosity - directly affects quality and volume of target_summary data passed to hmmrank
Restricts extraction to only top-scoring hit per profile; modifying this threshold changes number of sequences extracted and downstream analysis scope
groupTuple(sort: true) ensures consistent ordering of profiles and accession lists, critical for reproducible file naming and sequence extraction

checks_performed: hmmsearch produces valid target_summary files for each profile
hmmrank successfully consolidates and ranks results across all profiles
Rank filtering correctly identifies rank==1 entries
Accession numbers extracted from hmmrank match sequences in original FASTA
seqtk_subseq successfully retrieves all requested sequences
failure_modes: Empty hmmsearch results if profiles don't match sequences (no hits found)
hmmrank failure if target_summary files are malformed or missing
Accession number mismatches between hmmrank output and FASTA headers causing seqtk_subseq to fail
Duplicate accession numbers in filter files causing extraction errors
Memory issues if FASTA file is extremely large
recovery_actions: Validate HMM profiles and FASTA sequences are compatible (same sequence type: protein/DNA)
Check hmmsearch parameter flags for appropriate sensitivity settings
Verify FASTA header format matches accession number format in hmmrank output
Implement pre-filtering of hmmrank results by E-value threshold if too many hits
Process large FASTA files in chunks if memory constraints encountered

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTA_BUILD_ADD_KRAKEN2
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Build a custom Kraken2 database from FASTA sequences by adding sequences to a taxonomy database and compiling the final database
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/preprocessing stage - executed before taxonomic classification workflows
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: FASTA sequences, NCBI taxonomy files (names.dmp, nodes.dmp), accession-to-taxid mapping file, and optionally a custom sequence ID to taxid mapping file

component_tools.role: Adds FASTA sequences to the Kraken2 library with taxonomic annotations using accession-to-taxid and optional custom seqid-to-taxid mappings
component_tools.why_chosen: Standardized nf-core module for reliable sequence-to-taxonomy mapping with support for both standard and custom identifiers

component_tools.role: Compiles the annotated library into a searchable Kraken2 database with optional intermediate file cleanup
component_tools.why_chosen: Official Kraken2 build process optimized for database compilation with configurable resource cleanup

data_flow.input: FASTA sequences (multiple files), NCBI taxonomy names.dmp, NCBI taxonomy nodes.dmp, accession-to-taxid mapping file, optional custom seqid-to-taxid mapping file, boolean flag for intermediate file cleanup
transformations: KRAKEN2_ADD: Maps FASTA sequences to taxonomy IDs using accession mappings and custom seqid mappings
KRAKEN2_ADD: Generates library files and seqid-to-taxid mapping output
KRAKEN2_BUILD: Compiles library into indexed k-mer database
KRAKEN2_BUILD: Optionally removes intermediate files based on val_cleanintermediate flag
data_flow.output: Compiled Kraken2 database directory with metadata, versions.yml file
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTA sequences → taxonomy-annotated library files → indexed Kraken2 database

use_patterns.scenario: Building custom Kraken2 database for specific organism set or custom reference genomes

subworkflow_overview.name: BAM_SUBSAMPLEDEPTH_SAMTOOLS
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Subsample a BAM/CRAM/SAM file to a target mean depth by calculating the current depth and computing an appropriate downsampling fraction
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline - post-alignment, pre-analysis
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Aligned BAM/CRAM/SAM file with corresponding index file (BAI/CRAI/CSI) and target depth value specified

component_tools.role: Calculates per-base depth across the BAM file to determine current sequencing depth
component_tools.why_chosen: Native samtools tool, efficient for depth calculation, integrates seamlessly with samtools ecosystem

component_tools.role: Parses depth output to compute mean depth across all positions
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight text processing, standard in bioinformatics pipelines, minimal dependencies

component_tools.role: Performs actual downsampling using calculated subsample fraction with -s parameter
component_tools.why_chosen: Integrated samtools functionality, supports multiple formats (BAM/CRAM/SAM), maintains index compatibility

data_flow.input: Channel containing: metadata, BAM/CRAM/SAM file path, index file path (BAI/CRAI/CSI), target depth value; Reference FASTA file
transformations: Step 1: Calculate per-base depth using samtools depth on input BAM
Step 2: Parse depth TSV output with gawk to extract mean depth value
Step 3: Calculate subsample fraction as (target_depth / mean_depth)
Step 4: Join original BAM channel with computed mean depth and subsample fraction
Step 5: Execute samtools view with subsample fraction to downsample reads
Step 6: Aggregate output BAM/CRAM/SAM with corresponding indices
data_flow.output: Subsampled BAM/CRAM/SAM file with matching index file (BAI/CRAI/CSI); version information
data_flow.format_conversions: Depth TSV → parsed Float value; BAM/CRAM/SAM format preserved through downsampling

use_patterns.scenario: Normalize sequencing depth across samples with variable coverage
use_patterns.upstream: BAM alignment, quality filtering, duplicate marking
use_patterns.downstream: Variant calling, copy number analysis, comparative genomics
use_patterns.variations: Target depth can vary by sample type (WGS: 30x, WES: 100x, targeted: 1000x)

use_patterns.scenario: Reduce computational burden for large BAM files
use_patterns.upstream: High-coverage sequencing data alignment
use_patterns.downstream: Faster variant calling, reduced storage requirements
use_patterns.variations: Can be applied iteratively to achieve specific depth targets

use_patterns.upstream: Multiple BAM files with different coverage depths
use_patterns.downstream: Performance evaluation, method comparison
use_patterns.variations: All samples normalized to same depth for fair comparison

parameter_interactions.interaction: GAWK calculates mean depth; SAMTOOLS_VIEW uses ratio of target_depth/mean_depth as subsample fraction (-s parameter)
Dynamically calculated per-sample; if fraction > 1.0, no downsampling occurs; if < 1.0, reads randomly excluded
Both tools auto-detect format; output format matches input format; index type (BAI/CRAI/CSI) determined by input
Required for CRAM format handling; optional for BAM but recommended for consistency

checks_performed: Verification that input BAM/CRAM/SAM file is valid and readable
Confirmation that index file exists and matches BAM file
Validation that depth calculation produces numeric output
Confirmation that computed subsample fraction is positive and finite
failure_modes: Corrupted or truncated BAM file causing samtools depth to fail
Missing or mismatched index file leading to samtools view failure
Empty BAM file resulting in zero mean depth (division by zero)
Target depth exceeding actual mean depth (subsample_fraction > 1.0, no downsampling)
Malformed depth TSV output preventing gawk parsing
recovery_actions: Validate BAM integrity with 'samtools quickcheck' before subworkflow
Regenerate index files if missing: 'samtools index'
Handle zero-depth case with conditional logic or minimum depth threshold
Allow subsample_fraction > 1.0 to pass through without modification (no downsampling needed)
Add error handling in gawk to skip malformed lines or provide default values
