Insufficient coverage at germline resource sites for accurate contamination estimation
recovery_actions: Review contamination table output and adjust filtermutectcalls parameters if needed
Verify interval file compatibility with reference genome
Ensure all reference files (FASTA, indices, dictionaries) are from same genome build
Increase sequencing depth or adjust germline resource sites if contamination estimation fails

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_NGSCHECKMATE
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Quality control workflow that verifies sample identity and detects potential sample mix-ups by analyzing SNP patterns across FASTQ files using NGSCheckMate
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/quality control stage - after initial FASTQ processing but before downstream analysis
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Input FASTQ files must be preprocessed and aligned; SNP panel file must be provided; samples should be from same or comparable sequencing platforms

component_tools.role: Extracts variant allele frequencies (VAF) from FASTQ files at predefined SNP positions
component_tools.why_chosen: Direct FASTQ processing enables early QC without requiring full alignment; NGSCheckMate is specialized for sample matching

component_tools.role: Compares VAF profiles across all samples to generate correlation matrix and identify matched/mismatched samples
component_tools.why_chosen: Aggregates individual sample VAFs into comparative analysis; produces standardized matching reports

data_flow.input: ch_fastq (channel with metadata and FASTQ files) and ch_snp_pt (channel with metadata and SNP panel file)
transformations: NGSCHECKMATE_FASTQ processes each FASTQ file against SNP panel to generate VAF files
VAF files are collected into single channel using map and collect operations
Collected VAFs are combined with SNP panel metadata
NGSCHECKMATE_VAFNCM performs pairwise correlation analysis on all VAF profiles
data_flow.output: corr_matrix (correlation matrix), matched (matched sample pairs), all (all comparisons), vaf (individual VAF files), pdf (optional visualization), versions (tool versions)
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTQ → VAF (variant allele frequency format) → correlation matrix and matching reports

use_patterns.upstream: FASTQ quality trimming, adapter removal, optional alignment
use_patterns.downstream: Sample exclusion/inclusion decisions, contamination assessment, downstream analysis with validated samples
use_patterns.variations: Can process single sample (generates self-correlation), multiple batches (separate SNP panels), or mixed sample types

use_patterns.upstream: Raw or minimally processed FASTQ files
use_patterns.downstream: Investigation of discordant samples, re-sequencing decisions
use_patterns.variations: Can use different SNP panels for different organisms or tissue types

parameter_interactions.interaction: SNP panel defines which positions are interrogated; same panel must be used for all samples to enable comparison; .first() ensures single panel is used across all samples
Metadata is preserved through VAF generation and used for output tracking and correlation matrix labeling
Correlation matrix size scales with number of samples; pairwise comparisons increase quadratically

checks_performed: SNP coverage verification at defined positions
VAF consistency across replicates
Sample correlation coefficient calculation
Identification of matched sample pairs above correlation threshold
Detection of unexpected sample relationships
failure_modes: Insufficient SNP coverage in FASTQ files (low sequencing depth)
SNP panel incompatibility with sample type or organism
Complete sample mix-ups or contamination (low correlation with expected matches)
Missing or corrupted FASTQ files
Metadata inconsistencies between input channels
recovery_actions: Verify SNP panel matches sample organism and sequencing platform
Check FASTQ file quality and sequencing depth
Investigate low correlation scores for expected matches
Re-run with alternative SNP panel if organism mismatch suspected
Validate sample identities through alternative methods if discordance detected

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_ALIGN_MAPAD
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Align FASTQ reads against a reference genome using mapAD (aDNA short-read aligner), producing sorted, indexed BAM files with comprehensive alignment statistics
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline - follows quality control and precedes variant calling or downstream analysis
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Quality-controlled FASTQ files, pre-built mapAD index files, reference FASTA sequence (optional but recommended)

component_tools.role: Performs the core alignment of FASTQ reads to reference genome using mapAD algorithm optimized for ancient DNA
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized for aDNA with damage pattern modeling and short-read handling capabilities

component_tools.role: Sorts BAM file by genomic coordinates for efficient downstream processing
component_tools.why_chosen: Standard, reliable, integrated into BAM_SORT_STATS_SAMTOOLS subworkflow

component_tools.role: Creates BAI or CSI index files for rapid random access to BAM records
component_tools.why_chosen: Essential for indexed BAM format, included in BAM_SORT_STATS_SAMTOOLS subworkflow

component_tools.role: Generates comprehensive alignment statistics including coverage, insert size distribution, and quality metrics
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight, fast, standard output format for quality assessment

component_tools.role: Produces summary statistics on read flags (mapped, unmapped, paired, etc.)
component_tools.why_chosen: Quick overview of alignment success rates and read categories

component_tools.role: Reports per-chromosome mapping statistics including mapped and unmapped read counts
component_tools.why_chosen: Identifies reference-specific coverage distribution

component_tools.role: Orchestrates sorting, indexing, and statistical analysis of BAM files
component_tools.why_chosen: Encapsulates best practices and ensures consistent output across pipeline

data_flow.input: FASTQ reads (ch_reads with mandatory single_end metadata), mapAD index files (ch_index), optional reference FASTA (ch_fasta), and 9 mapAD algorithm parameters
transformations: Combine reads and index channels to create read-reference pairs
Generate composite metadata keys (key_read_ref) combining sample and reference IDs to prevent file overwrites
Preserve index ID in metadata (id_index) for multi-reference scenarios
Separate combined channel into reads and index streams via multiMap
Execute mapAD alignment with aDNA-specific parameters
Sort aligned BAM by coordinate
Create BAI/CSI indices for sorted BAM
Generate alignment statistics (stats, flagstat, idxstats)
data_flow.output: Unsorted BAM (bam_unsorted), sorted indexed BAM (bam), index files (bai/csi), and three statistical files (stats, flagstat, idxstats)
data_flow.format_conversions: SAM → BAM (via mapAD), unsorted BAM → sorted BAM (via samtools sort)

use_patterns.upstream: FASTQ quality control, reference indexing with mapAD
use_patterns.downstream: Variant calling, coverage analysis, or BAM merging
use_patterns.variations: Minimal - straightforward one-to-one mapping

use_patterns.upstream: Multiple pre-built mapAD indices for different references
use_patterns.downstream: Reference-specific variant calling or comparative analysis
use_patterns.variations: Metadata key_read_ref prevents output file collisions; requires careful index management

use_patterns.upstream: Batch FASTQ processing, single reference index
use_patterns.downstream: Joint variant calling or population-level analysis
use_patterns.variations: Channel broadcasting of single index across multiple samples

use_patterns.upstream: aDNA-specific quality control
use_patterns.downstream: Damage-aware variant calling
use_patterns.variations: Deamination rate parameters (val_deam_rate_double_stranded, val_deam_rate_single_stranded) configured for sample type

parameter_interactions.interaction: Controls alignment stringency; higher values allow more mismatches, affecting sensitivity vs. specificity trade-off
Boolean flag indicating library construction method; affects damage model application and scoring
Specify adapter overhang lengths for aDNA libraries; used in damage pattern modeling
Deamination rates for C→T transitions; critical for aDNA damage modeling and quality scoring
Controls indel penalty in alignment scoring; affects gap handling in short reads
When provided, enables reference-based statistics; when absent, statistics computed from BAM header only

checks_performed: Alignment rate via flagstat (percentage of mapped reads)
Per-chromosome coverage distribution via idxstats
Insert size distribution and quality score metrics via stats
Presence of sorted and indexed BAM files
Metadata consistency across read-reference combinations
failure_modes: Extremely low mapping rate (<5%) indicating reference mismatch or poor read quality
Uneven chromosome coverage suggesting reference contamination or assembly issues
Missing index files preventing downstream random access
Metadata key collisions if id_index not properly configured in modules.conf
mapAD index corruption or incompatibility with reference
recovery_actions: Verify FASTQ quality and reference genome compatibility
Check mapAD index generation parameters match current reference
Ensure modules.conf includes meta.id_index prefix configuration
Validate reference FASTA integrity and index completeness
Review mapAD parameter settings for aDNA damage characteristics
Re-run BAM_SORT_STATS_SAMTOOLS if index generation failed

subworkflow_overview.name: BAM_QC_PICARD
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Produces comprehensive quality control statistics from BAM/CRAM files using Picard tools to assess alignment quality, coverage metrics, and sequencing performance
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/end of pipeline - post-alignment, pre-variant calling or final QC reporting
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Aligned BAM or CRAM files with corresponding BAI index files, reference FASTA with associated indices (FAI, DICT, GZI)

component_tools.role: Generates comprehensive alignment metrics including insert size distribution, quality score distribution, GC bias, and duplication metrics
component_tools.why_chosen: Picard provides standardized, comprehensive multi-metric output in single pass; widely used in production pipelines

component_tools.role: Calculates hybrid selection (targeted sequencing) metrics including on-target percentage, coverage uniformity, and enrichment statistics when bait and target intervals are provided
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized for targeted sequencing QC; provides standardized metrics for capture efficiency assessment

component_tools.role: Computes whole genome sequencing metrics including coverage distribution, GC bias, and genome-wide statistics for non-targeted samples
component_tools.why_chosen: Picard standard for WGS QC; provides consistent metrics across different sequencing strategies

data_flow.input: BAM/CRAM files with BAI indices, optional bait and target interval files, reference FASTA with FAI/DICT/GZI indices
transformations: Extract BAM/BAI from input tuple containing optional bait/target intervals
Branch samples into two paths: hsmetrics (when bait and target intervals present) and wgsmetrics (all others)
Run COLLECTMULTIPLEMETRICS on all samples with BAM/BAI and reference
Run COLLECTHSMETRICS on targeted samples with bait/target intervals and full reference indices
Run COLLECTWGSMETRICS on non-targeted samples with BAM/BAI and reference
data_flow.output: coverage_metrics (merged HS and WGS metrics), multiple_metrics (alignment quality metrics), versions
data_flow.format_conversions: BAM/CRAM input → Picard metrics text files (TSV-like format)

use_patterns.upstream: BAM alignment with bait and target interval files defined
use_patterns.downstream: Coverage analysis, variant calling with target-aware filtering
use_patterns.variations: Input includes non-empty bait_interval and target_interval arrays; triggers COLLECTHSMETRICS branch

use_patterns.upstream: BAM alignment without interval definitions
use_patterns.downstream: Genome-wide variant calling, population statistics
use_patterns.variations: Input has empty bait_interval and target_interval; triggers WGSMETRICS branch only

use_patterns.scenario: Mixed sample cohort (both targeted and WGS)
use_patterns.upstream: Multiple BAM files with varying interval definitions
use_patterns.downstream: Stratified QC reporting by sequencing type
use_patterns.variations: Branching logic automatically routes samples to appropriate metrics tool

parameter_interactions.interaction: Branching condition: if both intervals are non-empty, sample routes to HSMETRICS; otherwise routes to WGSMETRICS. Mutually exclusive execution paths.
COLLECTMULTIPLEMETRICS requires FAI only; COLLECTHSMETRICS requires all three (FAI, DICT, GZI); COLLECTWGSMETRICS requires FAI only. Index availability determines tool compatibility.
All tools accept both BAM and CRAM formats; CRAM requires reference for decompression but metrics output remains identical

checks_performed: Alignment quality metrics (mapping quality, insert size distribution)
Duplication rate assessment
GC bias detection
Coverage uniformity (for targeted sequencing)
On-target percentage (for targeted sequencing)
Genome-wide coverage distribution (for WGS)
failure_modes: Missing or corrupted BAI index files - causes tool failure
Mismatched reference FASTA - produces incorrect metrics
Invalid interval files (bait/target) - causes HSMETRICS failure
Insufficient disk space for temporary files - runtime error
Incompatible CRAM files without accessible reference - decompression failure
recovery_actions: Regenerate BAI indices using samtools index if missing
Verify reference FASTA matches alignment reference
Validate interval files format and coordinates
Ensure adequate temporary directory space
Provide accessible reference path for CRAM decompression

subworkflow_overview.name: fastq_create_umi_consensus_fgbio
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Identifies and removes UMI tags from FASTQ reads, converts them to unmapped BAM, maps to reference genome, groups UMIs, and generates consensus reads from each UMI group
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline - post-sequencing, pre-variant calling
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Raw FASTQ files with UMI tags, reference genome FASTA, reference dictionary file, optional pre-computed BWA index

component_tools.role: Converts FASTQ reads with UMI tags into tagged unmapped BAM (uBAM) files using read structure information
component_tools.why_chosen: Essential first step to preserve UMI information in structured BAM format for downstream processing

component_tools.role: Maps unmapped BAM reads to reference genome; used twice (pre and post consensus)
component_tools.why_chosen: Flexible aligner selection via parameter; bwa-mem2 offers improved performance on modern systems

component_tools.role: Creates reference genome index for alignment if not provided
component_tools.why_chosen: Required for BWA/BWA-MEM2 alignment; generated on-demand if iGenomes index unavailable

component_tools.role: Groups mapped reads by their UMI tags using specified strategy (e.g., Adjacency)
component_tools.why_chosen: Critical for identifying reads from same DNA molecule before consensus calling

component_tools.role: Generates consensus sequences from grouped UMI reads at molecular level
component_tools.why_chosen: Reduces sequencing errors by creating consensus from multiple reads of same molecule

component_tools.role: Creates duplex consensus from complementary strand pairs when duplex sequencing enabled
component_tools.why_chosen: Provides highest confidence consensus for duplex UMI protocols

component_tools.role: Filters consensus reads based on quality thresholds (base quality, error rate)
component_tools.why_chosen: Quality control step to remove low-confidence consensus sequences

component_tools.role: Merges multiple BAM files; used pre and post consensus generation
component_tools.why_chosen: Combines BAM outputs from parallel processing or multiple samples

component_tools.role: Converts BAM to FASTQ format for re-alignment; used pre and post consensus
component_tools.why_chosen: Standard format conversion for BWA input compatibility

component_tools.role: Sorts BAM files by coordinate for downstream processing
component_tools.why_chosen: Required for proper BAM indexing and tool compatibility

component_tools.role: BAM file filtering and format conversion
component_tools.why_chosen: Flexible BAM manipulation for quality filtering

component_tools.role: Creates BAM index files for random access
component_tools.why_chosen: Required for efficient BAM file querying by downstream tools

component_tools.role: Marks duplicate reads during alignment
component_tools.why_chosen: Integrated duplicate marking during BWA alignment phase

data_flow.input: FASTQ files with inline or read-name UMI tags, reference FASTA, reference dictionary, optional BWA index
transformations: FASTQ → unmapped BAM (uBAM) with UMI tags preserved
uBAM → FASTQ for alignment
FASTQ → aligned BAM (first mapping)
Aligned BAM → grouped by UMI
Grouped reads → molecular consensus BAM
Molecular consensus → duplex consensus BAM (if duplex=true)
Consensus BAM → filtered consensus BAM
Filtered consensus → FASTQ for second alignment
FASTQ → final aligned BAM (second mapping)
data_flow.output: Final consensus BAM file with UMI-deduplicated, error-corrected reads aligned to reference
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTQ↔BAM conversions occur at multiple stages; UMI tags embedded in BAM RX/QX fields

use_patterns.upstream: Raw sequencing data with UMI barcodes in reads
use_patterns.downstream: Variant calling, copy number analysis, or other genomic analyses
use_patterns.variations: Duplex vs simplex UMI structure; different grouping strategies (Adjacency, Edit-distance)

use_patterns.upstream: Paired-end reads with UMIs on both strands
use_patterns.downstream: High-confidence variant calls with reduced false positives
use_patterns.variations: duplex=true parameter enables callduplexconsensusreads step

use_patterns.upstream: Deep coverage of specific genomic regions with UMIs
use_patterns.downstream: Detection of rare variants or low-frequency mutations
use_patterns.variations: Adjusted min_reads thresholds for consensus calling

parameter_interactions.interaction: Selects between bwa-mem and bwa-mem2 for both pre and post-consensus alignments; determines which indexing module is executed
When true, enables duplex consensus calling; affects min_reads parameter interpretation (single vs three-value format)
Determines UMI grouping algorithm (Adjacency, Edit-distance, etc.); affects sensitivity of UMI group formation
Single integer for simplex; space-separated triplet for duplex; controls minimum reads required per UMI group for consensus
Minimum base quality threshold for consensus base calling; affects consensus accuracy
Maximum acceptable error rate in consensus reads; filters out low-quality consensus sequences post-generation
Optional pre-computed index; if provided, skips index generation; if absent, triggers on-demand indexing

checks_performed: UMI tag presence and format validation in fastqtobam step
Alignment quality filtering via samtools/view
Minimum read depth per UMI group (min_reads parameter)
Base quality thresholds during consensus calling (min_baseq)
Consensus sequence error rate filtering (max_base_error_rate)
Duplex strand agreement validation (when duplex=true)
failure_modes: Insufficient reads per UMI group - consensus not called
High error rates in consensus sequences - filtered out by filterconsensusreads
Mismatched read structure - UMI tags not properly extracted
Alignment failures - reads unmapped or poorly mapped
Duplex strand disagreement - consensus rejected for duplex mode
Missing reference index - indexing delays or failures
recovery_actions: Adjust min_reads threshold downward for lower-coverage regions
Relax max_base_error_rate if consensus quality acceptable
Verify read_structure parameter matches actual UMI position in reads
Check reference genome compatibility and alignment parameters
Review duplex protocol implementation if strand agreement fails
Pre-compute and provide bwa_index to avoid indexing bottlenecks

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTA_EXPLORE_SEARCH_PLOT_TIDK
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Identifies and visualizes the frequency of telomeric repeats along sliding windows in DNA sequences using both a priori (user-specified) and a posteriori (discovered) repeat sequences
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/analysis stage - processes quality-filtered FASTA files to generate telomere analysis reports
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Input FASTA file containing genomic sequences; optionally a user-specified telomeric repeat sequence for a priori analysis

component_tools.role: Filters out small sequences from input FASTA to remove noise and focus on meaningful sequences
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight, fast sequence filtering integrated into nf-core ecosystem

component_tools.role: Sorts filtered sequences by length for consistent processing and improved visualization
component_tools.why_chosen: Efficient sorting maintains sequence metadata and integrates with nf-core modules

component_tools.role: Discovers the most frequent telomeric repeat sequence a posteriori by analyzing sequence composition
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized tool designed specifically for telomere repeat discovery

component_tools.role: Searches for user-specified a priori telomeric repeat sequences and generates frequency TSV reports
component_tools.why_chosen: Optimized for sliding window telomere repeat quantification with standardized output

component_tools.role: Searches for discovered a posteriori telomeric repeat sequences using top sequence from TIDK_EXPLORE
component_tools.why_chosen: Enables comparison between user-specified and discovered repeat patterns

component_tools.role: Generates SVG visualizations of a priori telomeric repeat frequency distributions
component_tools.why_chosen: Produces publication-quality SVG plots optimized for telomere data visualization

component_tools.role: Generates SVG visualizations of a posteriori telomeric repeat frequency distributions
component_tools.why_chosen: Enables visual comparison of discovered versus specified repeat patterns

transformations: Filter sequences by length using seqkit/seq
Sort filtered sequences by length using seqkit/sort
Explore and discover top telomeric repeat sequence using tidk/explore
Search for a priori repeat sequences in sorted FASTA, generate TSV results
Search for a posteriori (discovered) repeat sequences in sorted FASTA, generate TSV results
Plot a priori search results as SVG visualization
Plot a posteriori search results as SVG visualization
data_flow.output: apriori_tsv, apriori_svg, aposteriori_sequence (txt), aposteriori_tsv, aposteriori_svg
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTA → filtered FASTA → sorted FASTA; TSV data → SVG plots; text sequence file extracted to string

use_patterns.scenario: Comparative telomere analysis with known repeat sequences
use_patterns.upstream: Quality-controlled FASTA file from genome assembly or sequencing pipeline
use_patterns.downstream: Statistical comparison of a priori vs a posteriori results; publication of telomere frequency plots
use_patterns.variations: Can run with or without a priori sequence; if omitted, only a posteriori analysis performed

use_patterns.scenario: Discovery of novel telomeric repeats in non-model organisms
use_patterns.upstream: Assembled or long-read sequenced genomic DNA
use_patterns.downstream: Validation of discovered repeats; phylogenetic comparison across species
use_patterns.variations: Focus on a posteriori results when a priori sequence unknown

use_patterns.scenario: Telomere length and composition profiling across multiple genomes
use_patterns.upstream: Multiple FASTA files processed in parallel
use_patterns.downstream: Aggregation of TSV results for comparative genomics analysis
use_patterns.variations: Batch processing with consistent filtering parameters

parameter_interactions.interaction: If provided, enables a priori search branch; if empty (Channel.empty()), a priori analysis is skipped via join operation
Smaller threshold retains more sequences but may include noise; larger threshold focuses on major sequences but may miss important telomeres

parameter_interactions.parameter: sliding window size (implicit in TIDK modules)

checks_performed: Sequence length filtering removes short/low-quality sequences

Metadata ID matching between ch_fasta and ch_apriori_sequence ensures correct pairing
TSV output validation before plotting (implicit in TIDK_PLOT modules)

Sequence text file not properly stripped of whitespace causes search failures

Verify ch_apriori_sequence metadata IDs match ch_fasta IDs exactly
Provide explicit a priori sequence if a posteriori discovery fails
Check TIDK version compatibility and input sequence format
Validate TSV intermediate outputs before plotting step

subworkflow_overview.name: UTILS_NFCORE_PIPELINE

subworkflow_overview.name: bam_methyldackel
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Quantifies methylation levels (5-methylcytosine) from bisulfite-converted DNA alignments using Methyldackel, analyzing C-to-T conversion patterns in 3-letter genome BAM files

component_tools.why_chosen: Methyldackel is optimized for 3-letter genome analysis and provides multiple output formats for downstream analysis

component_tools.role: Calculates and visualizes methylation bias across read positions to identify systematic biases in methylation calls
component_tools.why_chosen: Integrated quality control to detect position-specific methylation artifacts common in bisulfite sequencing

subworkflow_overview.name: BAM_TAPS_CONVERSION
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Assess C->T conversion rates as a readout for methylation status across the genome using TAPS (Thermostable Alkaline Phosphatase-mediated Sequencing) methodology
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/post-alignment
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Aligned BAM files with corresponding BAI indices and reference genome FASTA with index

component_tools.role: Calculates molecular bias (MBIAS) metrics from BAM alignments to quantify C->T conversion efficiency
component_tools.why_chosen: Rastair is optimized for TAPS-specific C->T conversion analysis with 4-letter genome support

component_tools.role: Parses MBIAS output to extract clipping parameters (nOT_clip, nOB_clip) for bias correction
component_tools.why_chosen: Provides standardized extraction of bias metrics needed for downstream methylation calling

component_tools.role: Performs methylation calling using BAM files and bias-corrected parameters to generate methylation calls
component_tools.why_chosen: Integrates MBIAS correction directly into calling pipeline for improved accuracy

component_tools.role: Converts methylation calls to MethylKit-compatible format for statistical analysis and visualization
component_tools.why_chosen: Enables downstream statistical analysis in R/MethylKit ecosystem

data_flow.input: BAM files with indices (ch_bam, ch_bai) and reference genome FASTA with index (ch_fasta, ch_fasta_index)
transformations: RASTAIR_MBIAS: BAM + reference → MBIAS metrics (txt)
RASTAIR_MBIASPARSER: MBIAS metrics → clipping parameters (nOT_clip, nOB_clip)
RASTAIR_CALL: BAM + reference + clipping parameters → methylation calls (txt)
RASTAIR_METHYLKIT: methylation calls → MethylKit format (txt.gz)
data_flow.output: Three output channels: mbias (raw bias metrics), call (methylation calls), methylkit (formatted for analysis)
data_flow.format_conversions: Text-based MBIAS metrics → parsed parameters → methylation call format → compressed MethylKit format

use_patterns.upstream: BAM alignment from TAPS-treated sequencing data
use_patterns.downstream: Statistical analysis in R/MethylKit, differential methylation analysis, visualization
use_patterns.variations: Can be applied to single-end or paired-end TAPS sequencing data

use_patterns.scenario: Quality assessment of TAPS conversion efficiency
use_patterns.upstream: Aligned BAM files from TAPS experiment
use_patterns.downstream: MBIAS plots and conversion rate reports
use_patterns.variations: Focus on mbias output for QC without proceeding to methylation calling

use_patterns.upstream: Multiple TAPS samples aligned to reference
use_patterns.downstream: Comparative methylation analysis across samples
use_patterns.variations: Batch processing of multiple samples with aggregated statistics

Strand-specific bias quantification (OT vs OB strands)
Methylation call confidence based on conversion rates
Format validation in MethylKit conversion
failure_modes: Low C->T conversion rates indicating failed TAPS treatment
Severe strand bias suggesting technical artifacts
Missing or corrupted BAM/BAI files
Reference genome mismatch or missing index
Insufficient read coverage for reliable methylation calls
recovery_actions: Review MBIAS plots to identify conversion efficiency issues
Check BAM file integrity and re-align if necessary
Verify reference genome matches alignment reference
Increase sequencing depth if coverage is limiting
Adjust clipping parameters if bias is extreme

component_tools.role: Creates Bowtie2-format index for fast short-read alignment

use_patterns.downstream: dragmap/align module using hash table
use_patterns.variations: No ALT contig support; standalone indexing

subworkflow_overview.name: H5AD_REMOVEBACKGROUND_BARCODES_CELLBENDER_ANNDATA

component_tools.role: Filters the original h5ad file to retain only barcodes identified as valid cells by CellBender
component_tools.why_chosen: Provides standardized AnnData-compatible barcode filtering that maintains data integrity and metadata

subworkflow_overview.name: DEEPVARIANT
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Calls genetic variants from next-generation DNA sequencing data using a deep neural network machine learning approach
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/core analysis stage
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Aligned BAM/CRAM files with indices, reference FASTA with indices (FAI, GZI), PAR BED file for sex chromosome handling, optional interval definitions

component_tools.role: Converts aligned reads into TFRecord examples and generates small model calls and gVCF outputs for neural network input
component_tools.why_chosen: Prepares data in optimal format for deep learning model; generates intermediate gVCF for postprocessing

component_tools.role: Applies pre-trained deep neural network model to TFRecord examples to generate variant call predictions
component_tools.why_chosen: Leverages Google's trained DeepVariant model for high-accuracy variant calling

component_tools.role: Converts neural network predictions into final VCF and gVCF outputs with proper formatting and indexing
component_tools.why_chosen: Integrates multiple DeepVariant outputs and applies reference-based filtering

CALLVARIANTS: Applies neural network to TFRecords producing variant call predictions

use_patterns.scenario: Standard whole genome or exome variant calling

use_patterns.downstream: Variant annotation (VEP, SnpEff), variant filtering, population genetics analysis

use_patterns.downstream: Sex-specific variant filtering using PAR regions
use_patterns.variations: PAR BED file required for proper handling of pseudoautosomal regions

Validate BAM/CRAM integrity with samtools quickcheck
Regenerate reference indices if missing

Ensure DeepVariant model files are accessible and correct version

subworkflow_overview.name: VCF_FILTER_BCFTOOLS_ENSEMBLVEP
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Filter VCF files using bcftools and/or Ensembl VEP filter_vep to remove unwanted variants based on quality criteria and functional annotations
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline, after variant calling and annotation
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: VCF file must be generated from variant calling; if using filter_vep, VCF must be annotated with VEP; feature file required for filter_vep filtering

component_tools.role: Performs fast initial filtering of VCF variants based on bcftools criteria (quality, genotype, region filters)
component_tools.why_chosen: Fast performance reduces variant count before slower filter_vep processing; bcftools is standard in nf-core

component_tools.role: Filters variants based on VEP annotations and functional impact using feature file criteria
component_tools.why_chosen: Comprehensive functional annotation filtering; integrates with Ensembl VEP pipeline

component_tools.role: Compresses filtered VCF output and creates tabix index for efficient downstream access
component_tools.why_chosen: Creates indexed VCF required for many downstream tools; standard nf-core module

data_flow.input: VCF file (ch_vcf: [meta, vcf]) and optional VEP feature file (ch_filter_vep_feature_file: [meta, txt])
transformations: If filter_with_bcftools=true: bcftools/view filters VCF based on quality/genotype criteria
If filter_with_filter_vep=true: ensemblvep/filtervep applies functional annotation filters to VCF
If filter_with_filter_vep=true: tabix/bgziptabix compresses and indexes filtered VCF
data_flow.output: Filtered VCF file (ch_vcf: [meta, vcf]) and corresponding tabix index (ch_tbi: [meta, tbi])
data_flow.format_conversions: VCF → (bcftools filtered VCF) → (filter_vep filtered VCF) → (bgzip compressed VCF + tabix index)

use_patterns.scenario: Both bcftools and filter_vep filtering enabled

use_patterns.downstream: Indexed filtered VCF for variant interpretation, association studies, or clinical reporting
use_patterns.variations: Can disable bcftools (filter_with_bcftools=false) for lenient filtering or disable filter_vep (filter_with_filter_vep=false) for quality-only filtering

use_patterns.downstream: Quality-filtered VCF without functional annotation filtering
use_patterns.variations: Useful when VEP annotation not available or functional filtering not needed

use_patterns.downstream: Functionally filtered VCF without quality-based filtering
use_patterns.variations: Useful when bcftools criteria already applied or quality filtering handled elsewhere

When true, filter_vep and tabix/bgziptabix execute; when false, these tools are skipped and bcftools output (if enabled) becomes final output

ensemblvep/filtervep validates VEP annotations against feature file criteria
tabix/bgziptabix verifies VCF compression and index creation

Insufficient disk space for bgzip compression

Verify feature file exists and is properly formatted
Validate input VCF with bcftools view -v
Ensure adequate disk space before running tabix/bgziptabix

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTA_BUILD_ADD_KRAKEN2_BRACKEN
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Build custom Kraken2 and optionally Bracken databases from FASTA sequences with taxonomic information

subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: FASTA sequences, NCBI taxonomy files (names.dmp, nodes.dmp), accession-to-taxid mapping file, optional custom seqid-to-taxid mapping

subworkflow_overview.name: VCF_IMPUTE_GLIMPSE
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Impute missing genotypes in VCF/BCF files using GLIMPSE (Genotype Likelihoods Imputation MethodS for Phasing and Estimation)
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline - post-variant calling, pre-downstream analysis
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Input VCF/BCF file with genotype likelihoods, reference panel VCF/BCF, sample information file, genetic map file, and pre-computed CSI indices

component_tools.role: Divides the genome into overlapping chunks for parallel phasing and imputation
component_tools.why_chosen: Enables efficient parallelization by creating optimal chunk boundaries with overlap regions

component_tools.role: Phases and imputes genotypes within each chunk using reference panel and genetic map
component_tools.why_chosen: GLIMPSE is optimized for low-coverage sequencing data and provides accurate imputation with computational efficiency

component_tools.role: Merges phased and imputed chunks into a single cohesive VCF/BCF file
component_tools.why_chosen: GLIMPSE ligate handles overlap regions correctly and maintains phase consistency across chunk boundaries

component_tools.role: Creates CSI indices for phased variants and final merged variants for efficient random access
component_tools.why_chosen: CSI indexing is required by GLIMPSE for subsequent operations and provides better performance for large files

GLIMPSE_CHUNK generates chunk definitions with region boundaries
Parse chunk TSV output to extract RegionIn and RegionOut coordinates
Combine chunk regions with original input data for phasing
GLIMPSE_PHASE processes each chunk independently with reference panel
Index phased variants with bcftools
Group phased variants by metadata and combine with indices
GLIMPSE_LIGATE merges all chunks into single file
Index final merged variants
data_flow.output: Chunk definitions file, merged imputed VCF/BCF file, and CSI index for merged variants
data_flow.format_conversions: TSV chunk file parsed to extract region coordinates; VCF/BCF files indexed to CSI format

use_patterns.upstream: Variant calling pipeline producing VCF with genotype likelihoods
use_patterns.downstream: Population genetics analysis, association studies, or variant annotation
use_patterns.variations: Can process single samples or cohorts; chunk size adjustable based on coverage and reference panel size

use_patterns.upstream: Joint genotyping of multiple samples with reference panel
use_patterns.downstream: GWAS, population structure analysis, or phased haplotype analysis
use_patterns.variations: Parallelization across chunks enables processing of large cohorts efficiently

use_patterns.upstream: Exome or targeted sequencing with sparse genotypes
use_patterns.downstream: Fine-mapping or functional variant analysis
use_patterns.variations: Region parameter restricts imputation to specific genomic intervals

Provides sample ploidy and population information; affects phasing accuracy and imputation quality
Provides recombination rates; critical for accurate phasing and imputation; must match reference panel coordinates
Provides haplotype information for imputation; quality and size directly impact imputation accuracy; index required for efficient access
Used as grouping key throughout workflow; enables sample tracking and parallel processing of multiple samples

Chunk boundary consistency verification during region parsing
Phased variant index creation after GLIMPSE_PHASE
Successful merging of all chunks with phase consistency checks
Final index creation on merged variants

Incompatible genetic map coordinates with reference panel
Sample information file format errors or missing samples
Chunk overlap region conflicts during ligation
Reference panel allele mismatches with input VCF
Insufficient memory for large chunks or cohorts
recovery_actions: Regenerate CSI index using bcftools index before rerunning
Validate genetic map and reference panel coordinate systems
Verify sample information file format matches GLIMPSE requirements
Reduce chunk size or increase memory allocation
Check reference panel and input VCF for consistent allele encoding
Implement checkpoint restart to resume from last successful chunk

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTA_INDEX_BISMARK_BWAMETH

component_tools.role: Generates bismark-specific genome index (methylation-aware bowtie2 index) when not provided
component_tools.why_chosen: Creates optimized index for bisulfite-converted read alignment specific to bismark workflow

Bismark index compression detection (branching on .gz extension)

subworkflow_overview.name: DIFFERENTIAL_FUNCTIONAL_ENRICHMENT

subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Completed differential abundance/expression analysis with ranked gene lists or differential statistics; prepared gene set databases; optional background gene lists

component_tools.role: Performs over-representation analysis (ORA) using g:Profiler database for functional term enrichment
component_tools.why_chosen: Comprehensive multi-source functional database with statistical testing for ORA

component_tools.role: Performs gene set enrichment analysis on ranked expression data; requires expression matrix, contrasts, and sample metadata
component_tools.why_chosen: Gold-standard method for pathway enrichment using ranked statistics without arbitrary cutoffs

component_tools.role: Pathway deconvolution and activity inference from expression data using multiple algorithms
component_tools.why_chosen: Unified framework for multiple deconvolution methods with regulatory network integration

component_tools.role: Proportionality-based gene set enrichment analysis for compositional data
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized for compositional/proportional data common in microbiome and RNA-seq

component_tools.role: Converts tabular gene expression data to GSEA GCT format (gene cluster text)

use_patterns.downstream: Functional term visualization, pathway network analysis

subworkflow_overview.name: MMSEQS_FASTA_CLUSTER

component_tools.why_chosen: Selected when higher sensitivity clustering is needed; slower but more accurate than linclust

component_tools.why_chosen: Selected for speed when processing large datasets; trades some sensitivity for performance

subworkflow_overview.name: BAM_VARIANT_CALLING_SORT_FREEBAYES_BCFTOOLS

component_tools.why_chosen: Haplotype-based variant caller suitable for population-scale variant discovery without requiring training data

Route to appropriate differential tool based on analysis_method parameter
Filter results using fc_threshold and stat_threshold parameters
data_flow.output: Differential abundance results per method-contrast combination with filtered tables; normalized abundance matrices; version information
data_flow.format_conversions: Count matrices converted to normalized/log-scale values; statistical results formatted as tabular data with filtering applied

use_patterns.scenario: Single analysis method with multiple contrasts
use_patterns.upstream: Abundance quantification producing count matrix
use_patterns.downstream: Result filtering and visualization of significant features
use_patterns.variations: Can iterate over multiple contrasts from same abundance matrix without re-normalization

use_patterns.upstream: Same abundance matrix and contrast definitions
use_patterns.downstream: Method comparison and consensus analysis
use_patterns.variations: Each method runs independently; results can be compared for consistency

use_patterns.scenario: Complex experimental designs with random effects
use_patterns.upstream: Metadata with batch/blocking variables
use_patterns.downstream: Variance-partitioned results accounting for design complexity
use_patterns.variations: Uses VARIANCEPARTITION_DREAM with formula parameter for random effects

use_patterns.upstream: Proportional abundance data without absolute counts
use_patterns.downstream: Compositionally-aware differential results
use_patterns.variations: Routes to PROPR_PROPD instead of count-based methods

parameter_interactions.interaction: Determines which differential analysis tool is invoked; stored in meta as 'differential_method' for downstream tracking
Passed to filter module to exclude features with fold-change below threshold; combined with stat_threshold for dual filtering
Passed to filter module to exclude features with p-value/adjusted p-value above threshold; combined with fc_threshold
Defines statistical model including random effects; only used when provided (optional); enables complex design handling
Optional input for length-bias correction; passed as empty file if unavailable using ternary operator
Optional input for negative control features; passed as empty file if unavailable; used for normalization reference

checks_performed: Metadata consistency across input channels via join operations
Presence of required samplesheet and abundance matrix
Optional file availability (transcript_lengths, control_features) with graceful empty file substitution
Contrast definition validity before cross-combination
Fold-change and statistical threshold application for result filtering
Method-specific quality metrics from each differential tool
failure_modes: Missing required metadata keys causing join failures
Incompatible contrast definitions with abundance matrix dimensions
Invalid analysis_method parameter routing to non-existent tool
Threshold parameters producing empty result sets (no significant features)
Mismatched sample names between samplesheet and abundance matrix
Optional files in wrong format when provided
recovery_actions: Validate metadata structure before workflow execution
Verify contrast definitions match sample groups in samplesheet
Use default analysis_method if invalid method specified
Adjust fc_threshold and stat_threshold if no results pass filtering
Check sample name consistency between input files
Provide optional files in expected format or omit entirely for empty file substitution

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_ALIGN_BWAALN
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Align FASTQ files against a reference genome using BWA aln short-read aligner, producing sorted and indexed BAM files
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline (post-QC, pre-variant calling)
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: FASTQ reads must be quality-checked; reference genome must be indexed with BWA; meta.single_end flag must be set in metadata

component_tools.role: Generates SAI (suffix array index) files from FASTQ reads against reference genome
component_tools.why_chosen: Optimized for short-read alignment; legacy but stable tool for Illumina data

component_tools.role: Converts paired-end SAI files to SAM format for paired-end reads
component_tools.why_chosen: Required for proper paired-end read assembly from two SAI files

component_tools.role: Converts single-end SAI files to SAM format for single-end reads
component_tools.why_chosen: Handles single-end read conversion when paired-end is not applicable

component_tools.role: Creates BAM index files (.bai) for efficient random access to aligned reads
component_tools.why_chosen: Enables downstream tools to quickly access specific genomic regions

data_flow.input: ch_reads: [val(meta), path(reads)] with meta.single_end flag; ch_index: [val(meta), path(index)]
transformations: Combine reads and index channels with cross-product
Create composite keys (key_read_ref) to track read-reference combinations
Branch SAI output by single_end flag into PE and SE paths
Join SAI files with original reads and index for conversion
Convert SAI to SAM (PE via sampe, SE via samse)
Index resulting BAM files
data_flow.output: Sorted and indexed BAM files with corresponding BAI index files
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTQ → SAI (bwa aln) → SAM (bwa sampe/samse) → BAM (implicit in samtools) → BAM + BAI (samtools index)

use_patterns.upstream: FASTQ quality control and reference genome preparation
use_patterns.downstream: BAM sorting, duplicate marking, variant calling
use_patterns.variations: Standard workflow with minimal metadata complexity

use_patterns.upstream: Batch FASTQ processing
use_patterns.downstream: Merged BAM files for cohort analysis
use_patterns.variations: Requires careful channel management to prevent file overwrites

use_patterns.scenario: Single or multiple samples against multiple reference genomes
use_patterns.upstream: Multiple reference genome indexing
use_patterns.downstream: Comparative alignment analysis
use_patterns.variations: Requires meta.id_index in modules.conf to prevent BAM file collisions; key_read_ref composite ID essential

use_patterns.upstream: Read type classification
use_patterns.downstream: Separate handling of PE and SE alignments
use_patterns.variations: Branching logic on meta.single_end flag handles both simultaneously

parameter_interactions.interaction: Boolean flag determines which SAM conversion tool is used; false routes to sampe (paired-end), true routes to samse (single-end)
Must be specified in modules.conf to create unique output filenames when multiple references are used; prevents BAM file overwrites
Combines meta.id and meta_index.id to uniquely identify read-reference combinations throughout workflow; enables correct association across multiple references

checks_performed: Metadata validation: meta.single_end flag presence required
Channel joining: ensures correct read-reference pairing via composite keys
SAI file generation: bwa aln must complete successfully before conversion
PE/SE branching: correct routing based on single_end flag
failure_modes: Missing meta.single_end flag causes incorrect branching
Duplicate BAM filenames when meta.id_index not configured for multiple references
Incorrect read-reference associations if composite key logic fails
SAI file corruption or missing files prevent SAM conversion
Index file generation failure prevents downstream random access
recovery_actions: Verify meta.single_end is set in input channel preparation
Configure meta.id_index in modules.conf before running with multiple references
Validate composite key generation in combine/map operations
Re-run bwa aln if SAI files are corrupted
Check disk space and permissions for index file creation

subworkflow_overview.name: BAM_MARKDUPLICATES_SAMTOOLS
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Mark duplicate reads in SAM/BAM/CRAM files using samtools, preparing alignment files for downstream analysis by identifying and flagging PCR duplicates
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline, after alignment and before variant calling or other analyses
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Aligned SAM/BAM/CRAM file from aligner (e.g., bwa, bowtie2); reference FASTA file for coordinate validation

component_tools.role: Collates BAM file by read name to group paired-end reads together, preparing for fixmate operation
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight, fast preprocessing step that organizes reads by name for efficient duplicate detection in paired-end data

component_tools.role: Fills in mate coordinate and insert size fields, correcting mate information after collation
component_tools.why_chosen: Essential for accurate duplicate marking; ensures mate pair information is consistent and complete

component_tools.role: Sorts BAM file by genomic coordinates, organizing reads for efficient duplicate detection and downstream processing
component_tools.why_chosen: Coordinate sorting is required for markdup to work correctly; samtools sort is efficient and integrates seamlessly

component_tools.role: Identifies and flags duplicate reads based on 5' mapping positions and insert sizes, setting duplicate flag in BAM
component_tools.why_chosen: Native samtools implementation; fast, memory-efficient, and produces standard SAM duplicate flags compatible with all downstream tools

data_flow.input: Aligned BAM/SAM/CRAM file (channel: [val(meta), [bam]]) and reference FASTA file (channel: [val(meta), [fasta]])
transformations: Collate: Reorganize reads by name to group paired-end mates
Fixmate: Populate mate coordinate and insert size fields
Sort: Arrange reads by genomic coordinates
Markdup: Identify and flag duplicate reads based on mapping positions
data_flow.output: Duplicate-marked BAM file (channel: [val(meta), [bam]]) and version information
data_flow.format_conversions: No format conversion; input and output remain BAM format throughout

use_patterns.scenario: Standard whole genome sequencing (WGS) or whole exome sequencing (WES) pipeline
use_patterns.upstream: Alignment module (e.g., bwa mem, bowtie2) producing unsorted BAM with unmapped reads
use_patterns.downstream: Base quality score recalibration (BQSR), variant calling (GATK HaplotypeCaller, bcftools), or copy number analysis
use_patterns.variations: Can skip collate/fixmate if input is already name-sorted; can adjust markdup sensitivity parameters

use_patterns.upstream: RNA aligner output (STAR, hisat2)
use_patterns.downstream: Quantification, differential expression analysis
use_patterns.variations: May use alternative duplicate marking strategies for RNA-seq; some workflows skip this step entirely

use_patterns.upstream: Alignment of amplicon reads
use_patterns.downstream: Variant calling with duplicate-aware tools
use_patterns.variations: May require adjusted parameters for high-depth amplicon data; consider UMI-based deduplication as alternative

parameter_interactions.interaction: Reference file used for coordinate validation and sorting; must match the reference used for alignment to ensure correct duplicate detection
Indicates no additional sort options; sorts by default coordinate order (chromosome, position)
Propagated through all steps to maintain sample identity and attributes; critical for multi-sample processing

checks_performed: Mate pair information consistency (fixmate validation)
Coordinate sorting correctness (sort validation)
Duplicate detection accuracy based on 5' positions and insert sizes
BAM file integrity after each step
failure_modes: Corrupted or truncated input BAM file causing collate/fixmate failure
Reference FASTA mismatch leading to incorrect coordinate validation
Insufficient memory for large BAM files during sorting or duplicate detection
Malformed mate pair information in input preventing accurate fixmate operation
Duplicate flag conflicts if input already contains duplicate marks
recovery_actions: Validate input BAM integrity using 'samtools quickcheck'
Verify reference FASTA matches alignment reference using sequence checksums
Increase memory allocation for sort and markdup operations
Re-run alignment from raw reads if input BAM is corrupted
Clear existing duplicate flags before reprocessing if needed

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_SUBSAMPLE_FQ_SALMON
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Subsample FastQ files and perform pseudo-alignment with Salmon to infer library strandedness and generate quantification metrics
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Raw FastQ files, genome FASTA, transcript FASTA, GTF annotation file, and optionally a pre-built Salmon index

component_tools.role: Reduces FastQ file size by subsampling reads to a manageable subset for rapid analysis
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight, fast subsampling tool integrated into nf-core ecosystem for consistent performance

component_tools.role: Builds a Salmon index from genome and transcript FASTA files for pseudo-alignment
component_tools.why_chosen: Salmon is optimized for fast pseudo-alignment and strandedness inference; conditional execution allows reuse of existing indices

component_tools.role: Performs pseudo-alignment of subsampled reads and generates quantification results with library format detection
component_tools.why_chosen: Salmon provides accurate strandedness detection through lib_format_counts output and fast pseudo-alignment without full BAM generation

data_flow.input: ch_reads (FastQ files with metadata), ch_genome_fasta, ch_transcript_fasta, ch_gtf, ch_index (optional), make_index (boolean flag)
transformations: Conditionally create Salmon index from genome and transcript FASTA if make_index=true
Subsample input FastQ files using FQ_SUBSAMPLE
Pseudo-align subsampled reads to index using SALMON_QUANT with automatic library type detection (lib_type='A')
data_flow.output: Subsampled FastQ files, Salmon quantification results directory, JSON info files, library format counts (for strandedness inference), Salmon index, version information
data_flow.format_conversions: FastQ → subsampled FastQ → Salmon quantification (no BAM output, pseudo-alignment only)

use_patterns.scenario: Rapid strandedness detection on large datasets
use_patterns.upstream: Raw FastQ files from sequencing, reference genome and annotations
use_patterns.downstream: Strandedness determination from lib_format_counts, full pipeline re-run with correct strand parameter
use_patterns.variations: Can skip index creation if pre-built index provided; subsample size can be adjusted via FQ_SUBSAMPLE parameters

use_patterns.upstream: Initial FastQ QC (FastQC, MultiQC)
use_patterns.downstream: Full Salmon quantification or other alignment-based quantification with determined parameters
use_patterns.variations: Results can inform decision to proceed with full analysis or troubleshoot sample issues

parameter_interactions.interaction: When true, SALMON_INDEX is executed and its output index is passed to SALMON_QUANT; when false, pre-built ch_index is used directly, skipping index creation
Set to 'A' (automatic) to enable Salmon's library type detection; output lib_format_counts reveals actual strandedness for downstream configuration
Set to false for pseudo-alignment mode (faster, no BAM output); true would enable alignment-based mode requiring BAM input

checks_performed: Salmon index validity (implicit via SALMON_INDEX module)
FastQ subsampling success (FQ_SUBSAMPLE output validation)
Pseudo-alignment completion and read mapping rates (via Salmon logs)
Library format detection confidence (lib_format_counts JSON analysis)
failure_modes: Invalid or corrupted input FASTA files preventing index creation
Insufficient reads in FastQ files for meaningful subsampling
Mismatched transcript FASTA and GTF annotations causing alignment failures
Ambiguous library format detection (low confidence strandedness inference)
recovery_actions: Validate input FASTA/GTF files with sequence integrity checks
Increase subsample size or use full FastQ if subsampling fails
Verify GTF and FASTA coordinate systems match (same genome build)
Inspect lib_format_counts JSON; if ambiguous, manually specify strand in downstream analysis or increase sample depth

subworkflow_overview.name: UTILS_REFERENCES
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Utility subworkflow for extracting and managing reference files and values from YAML reference configurations and parameters
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: start/initialization
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Valid YAML reference file with schema compliance, schema_references.json must exist in subworkflows/nf-core/utils_references/

component_tools.role: Parses YAML reference file into structured list format using JSON schema validation
component_tools.why_chosen: Part of nf-schema plugin, provides schema validation and standardized parsing

component_tools.role: Extracts file paths from references, resolves parameter substitutions, validates file existence
component_tools.why_chosen: Handles conditional logic for parameter override and path resolution with checkIfExists validation

component_tools.role: Extracts scalar values from references with parameter override capability
component_tools.why_chosen: Provides consistent interface for value extraction with parameter precedence

transformations: Parse YAML reference file using samplesheetToList with schema validation
Create Channel from parsed references list
Map references to extract file paths with parameter override logic
Resolve ${params.igenomes_base} placeholder with provided basepath
Validate file existence with checkIfExists
Map references to extract values with parameter override logic
Collect results into final output
data_flow.output: references_file (tuple of id metadata and validated file objects), references_value (tuple of id metadata and extracted values)

use_patterns.scenario: Extracting reference genome files from iGenomes configuration
use_patterns.upstream: Pipeline initialization, parameter validation
use_patterns.downstream: Alignment tools, annotation tools that require reference files
use_patterns.variations: Custom basepath for non-iGenomes references, parameter override for specific samples

use_patterns.scenario: Extracting reference metadata values (species, build version)
use_patterns.upstream: Reference YAML parsing
use_patterns.downstream: Logging, report generation, downstream tool configuration
use_patterns.variations: Parameter-based override for custom values, conditional attribute selection

parameter_interactions.interaction: When provided, overrides attribute_file value from metadata; takes precedence in conditional logic
When provided, overrides attribute_value from metadata; takes precedence in conditional logic
Replaces ${params.igenomes_base} placeholder in file paths; enables custom reference locations
Specifies which metadata field to extract; used only if corresponding param is not provided

checks_performed: YAML schema validation via schema_references.json
File existence validation with checkIfExists: true
Null filtering for missing attributes and parameters
failure_modes: YAML parsing failure if schema_references.json missing or invalid
File not found error if referenced file does not exist at resolved path
Null values returned if both parameter and attribute are missing
Path resolution failure if ${params.igenomes_base} placeholder cannot be replaced
recovery_actions: Verify schema_references.json exists in correct location
Validate basepath parameter points to accessible directory
Ensure YAML reference file contains required attributes
Provide param_file or param_value as fallback when metadata attributes missing

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_ALIGN_BOWTIE2
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Align FASTQ reads to a reference genome using Bowtie2, then sort, index, and generate quality statistics on the resulting BAM file
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle of pipeline - after quality control and before variant calling or downstream analysis
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Bowtie2 index files must be pre-built; reference FASTA file must be available; input FASTQ reads must be quality-controlled

component_tools.role: Performs the core read alignment to reference genome, producing BAM output and alignment logs
component_tools.why_chosen: Bowtie2 is optimized for short-read alignment with good speed and accuracy; widely used in nf-core pipelines

component_tools.role: Composite subworkflow that sorts BAM, creates indices, and generates alignment statistics
component_tools.why_chosen: Encapsulates common BAM post-processing operations; ensures consistent quality metrics generation

component_tools.role: Sorts BAM file by genomic coordinates for efficient downstream processing
component_tools.why_chosen: Standard tool; required for indexing and most downstream analyses

component_tools.role: Creates BAI or CSI index files for rapid random access to BAM records
component_tools.why_chosen: Essential for efficient querying and visualization of alignment data

component_tools.role: Generates comprehensive alignment statistics including coverage, insert size, and quality metrics
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight, fast, and provides detailed alignment quality information

component_tools.role: Reports per-chromosome read counts and unmapped reads for quick alignment overview
component_tools.why_chosen: Fast summary statistics; useful for detecting alignment bias across chromosomes

component_tools.role: Provides summary of read flags (paired, mapped, duplicates, etc.) for quality assessment
component_tools.why_chosen: Standard QC metric; quickly identifies mapping issues

data_flow.input: ch_reads (FASTQ files with metadata), ch_index (Bowtie2 index directory), ch_fasta (reference FASTA), save_unaligned (boolean), sort_bam (boolean)
transformations: FASTQ reads aligned to reference genome using Bowtie2 index
Aligned BAM file sorted by genomic coordinates
Sorted BAM indexed with BAI/CSI indices
Alignment statistics generated (stats, flagstat, idxstats)
Unaligned reads optionally saved as FASTQ
data_flow.output: bam (sorted aligned BAM), bai/csi (index files), stats (alignment statistics), flagstat (flag summary), idxstats (per-chromosome counts), log_out (alignment logs), fastq (unaligned reads if requested), versions (tool versions)
data_flow.format_conversions: FASTQ → SAM (via Bowtie2) → BAM (via samtools) → sorted BAM with indices

use_patterns.upstream: FASTQ quality control, adapter trimming, Bowtie2 index building
use_patterns.downstream: Variant calling (GATK, bcftools), copy number analysis, or peak calling
use_patterns.variations: sort_bam parameter controls whether Bowtie2 outputs pre-sorted BAM; save_unaligned captures unmapped reads for troubleshooting

use_patterns.upstream: Quality trimming, Bowtie2 index from target genome
use_patterns.downstream: Peak calling (MACS2), quality filtering by flagstat/idxstats
use_patterns.variations: May use stricter filtering based on flagstat metrics; idxstats used to verify on-target alignment

use_patterns.upstream: Initial FASTQ files, reference genome
use_patterns.downstream: Analysis of stats/flagstat/idxstats to identify contamination or mapping issues
use_patterns.variations: save_unaligned=true to capture and re-align problematic reads; examine log_out for alignment rate issues

parameter_interactions.interaction: When true, Bowtie2 outputs unaligned reads as FASTQ for downstream re-alignment or contamination analysis; when false, unaligned reads are discarded
When true, Bowtie2 outputs pre-sorted BAM reducing downstream sorting overhead; when false, BAM_SORT_STATS_SAMTOOLS performs sorting
Reference FASTA used by Bowtie2 for alignment and by samtools stats for generating per-chromosome statistics; must match the Bowtie2 index

checks_performed: Alignment rate from Bowtie2 log (percentage of reads successfully aligned)
Flagstat metrics (properly paired reads, singletons, duplicates, QC failures)
Idxstats per-chromosome distribution (detects contamination or off-target alignment)
Samtools stats coverage and insert size metrics (identifies sequencing or library prep issues)
BAM index creation success (validates BAM integrity)
failure_modes: Low alignment rate (<70%) indicates poor read quality, contamination, or wrong reference genome
High duplicate rate (>20%) suggests PCR over-amplification or low complexity library
Uneven chromosome distribution in idxstats suggests contamination or reference mismatch
Failed index creation indicates corrupted BAM file from Bowtie2
Extreme insert size values indicate library preparation problems
recovery_actions: If low alignment: check FASTQ quality, verify reference genome matches sample, re-trim adapters
If high duplicates: mark duplicates with Picard or samtools, consider UMI-based deduplication
If uneven distribution: investigate contamination source, verify index matches reference
If index fails: re-run Bowtie2 alignment with diagnostic logging
If insert size anomalies: review library preparation protocol, check for chimeric reads

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTQ_GENERATE_STATISTICS
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Generate comprehensive quality control statistics for short read sequencing data using multiple complementary tools to provide diverse analytical perspectives
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: early/middle stage of pipeline, immediately after read input or demultiplexing
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Raw FASTQ files must be available; metadata (sample names, read types) should be prepared in channel format

component_tools.role: Generates HTML quality reports with per-base quality scores, GC content, adapter contamination detection, and sequence duplication levels
component_tools.why_chosen: Industry standard for FASTQ QC; produces visual HTML reports; widely recognized output format

component_tools.role: Performs basic FASTQ validation and integrity checks; identifies malformed records
component_tools.why_chosen: Lightweight validation tool; part of seqfu suite; quick error detection

component_tools.role: Calculates read length distribution, base composition, and quality statistics; generates MultiQC-compatible output
component_tools.why_chosen: Produces MultiQC-compatible reports; comprehensive statistics; part of unified seqfu toolkit

component_tools.role: Generates summary statistics including read count, total bases, min/max/mean length, and GC percentage
component_tools.why_chosen: Fast performance; simple tabular output; good for quick summaries

component_tools.role: Computes nucleotide composition (A, T, G, C, N counts) and base frequency analysis
component_tools.why_chosen: Specialized composition analysis; lightweight; standard bioinformatics tool

data_flow.input: ch_reads: channel containing [val(meta), [fastq]] tuples with sample metadata and FASTQ file paths
transformations: FASTQC: FASTQ → HTML report + ZIP archive with detailed quality metrics
SEQFU_CHECK: FASTQ → validation report identifying format issues
SEQFU_STATS: FASTQ → statistics file + MultiQC-compatible JSON
SEQKIT_STATS: FASTQ → tabular summary statistics
SEQTK_COMP: FASTQ → nucleotide composition table

use_patterns.scenario: Standard QC pipeline for whole genome sequencing
use_patterns.upstream: Read demultiplexing, adapter trimming (optional)
use_patterns.downstream: MultiQC aggregation, read filtering/trimming based on QC results, alignment
use_patterns.variations: All tools enabled; typically used with skip_* parameters set to false

use_patterns.scenario: Rapid QC assessment with minimal overhead
use_patterns.upstream: Raw FASTQ input
use_patterns.downstream: Decision point for read quality acceptance
use_patterns.variations: Enable only SEQKIT_STATS and SEQFU_CHECK; skip FASTQC and SEQTK_COMP for speed

use_patterns.scenario: Detailed composition analysis for contamination detection
use_patterns.upstream: Demultiplexed reads
use_patterns.downstream: Contamination assessment, species identification
use_patterns.variations: Prioritize SEQTK_COMP output; enable all tools for comprehensive analysis

use_patterns.upstream: Multiple samples processed
use_patterns.downstream: MultiQC report generation
use_patterns.variations: Ensure seqfu_multiqc output is collected; disable tools that don't produce MultiQC-compatible formats if not needed

parameter_interactions.interaction: When true, FASTQC module is skipped entirely; fastqc_html and fastqc_zip outputs remain empty; no impact on other tools
When true, validation checks are skipped; seqfu_check output remains empty; does not affect downstream statistics generation
When true, seqfu_stats and seqfu_multiqc outputs are empty; MultiQC integration may be affected if this is primary source
When true, seqkit_stats output remains empty; does not affect other statistics tools
When true, seqtk_stats output remains empty; composition analysis unavailable; no cascading effects

checks_performed: FASTQC: Per-base quality scores, adapter contamination, sequence duplication, GC content distribution
SEQFU_CHECK: FASTQ format validity, record integrity, malformed sequence detection
SEQFU_STATS: Read length distribution, base composition balance, quality score distribution
SEQKIT_STATS: Read count thresholds, total base count, length range validation
SEQTK_COMP: Nucleotide frequency anomalies, N-content levels, GC percentage extremes
failure_modes: Corrupted FASTQ files detected by SEQFU_CHECK
Extremely low quality scores across reads (FASTQC)
High adapter contamination (FASTQC)
Abnormal GC content suggesting contamination (FASTQC, SEQTK_COMP)
Excessive N-content indicating sequencing failures (SEQTK_COMP)
Unusual read length distribution (SEQFU_STATS, SEQKIT_STATS)
Zero or very low read counts (SEQKIT_STATS)
recovery_actions: Review FASTQC HTML reports for visual assessment of quality issues
Check SEQFU_CHECK output for format errors; re-validate input files
Compare SEQTK_COMP composition against expected organism baseline
Use SEQFU_STATS length distribution to identify trimming requirements
Cross-reference all tool outputs to distinguish systematic vs. random issues
Consider re-sequencing if multiple tools indicate severe quality problems
Implement read filtering/trimming based on identified issues before downstream analysis

subworkflow_overview.name: FASTA_GXF_BUSCO_PLOT
subworkflow_overview.purpose: Evaluates completeness of genome assemblies and their gene annotations using BUSCO, generating comparative summary plots for both assembly and annotation quality assessment
subworkflow_overview.typical_position: middle/end of genome annotation pipeline
subworkflow_overview.prerequisites: Assembled genome FASTA file and corresponding GFF/GFF3/GTF annotation file with matching metadata IDs

component_tools.role: Assesses completeness of genome assemblies and protein annotations against lineage-specific gene databases
component_tools.why_chosen: Industry standard for genome completeness assessment with lineage-specific benchmarks

component_tools.role: Creates visual summary plots comparing BUSCO results across multiple runs and lineages
component_tools.why_chosen: Native BUSCO plotting utility ensures consistent visualization of BUSCO metrics

component_tools.role: Extracts protein sequences from GFF/GTF annotations for protein-mode BUSCO evaluation

transformations: Combine FASTA with BUSCO mode and lineage parameters

Run BUSCO on assembly in specified mode (genome/transcriptome)
Run BUSCO on extracted proteins in protein mode (if assembly mode is genome)
Generate comparative plots from BUSCO results

use_patterns.scenario: Multi-lineage BUSCO comparison across different taxonomic groups
use_patterns.upstream: Multiple genome assemblies with consistent annotation format
use_patterns.downstream: Phylogenetic placement or taxonomic confirmation
use_patterns.variations: val_lineages parameter accepts multiple lineages for comprehensive assessment

parameter_interactions.interaction: Controls BUSCO evaluation mode for assembly (genome/transcriptome/proteins); if mode is 'genome', annotation is evaluated in 'proteins' mode; other modes skip annotation evaluation
Determines which BUSCO lineage databases to use; creates separate evaluation runs for each lineage via channel.fromList()
Optional custom path to BUSCO lineage databases; if provided, overrides default BUSCO database location; combined via channel.of()
Optional BUSCO configuration file for custom parameters; applied to all BUSCO runs if provided
Boolean flag controlling removal of BUSCO intermediate files; reduces storage footprint when set to true

checks_performed: BUSCO completeness score for assembly (single-copy, duplicated, fragmented, missing BUSCOs)
BUSCO completeness score for gene annotation proteins
